title: [BUG] pricing registry doesn't match OpenRouter routes that include a vendor prefix in the model id (e.g. `google/gemini-2.5-flash`)
body:
### Describe the Bug

# Bug: pricing registry doesn't match OpenRouter routes that include a vendor prefix in the model id (e.g. `google/gemini-2.5-flash`)

## Summary

When an Agent uses the OpenRouter gateway, the `MODEL_GENERATION` span records `model` as the full route id (e.g. `google/gemini-2.5-flash`), but the embedded pricing registry only contains entries for the bare model id (`gemini-2-5-flash`). As a result `estimateCosts` falls into the `no_matching_model` branch for **every** OpenRouter call that goes through a vendor sub-prefix, and Studio's "Total Model Cost" / "Model Usage & Cost" panels stay empty even though token metrics are correctly recorded.

This affects every OpenRouter route that has the form `openrouter/<vendor>/<model>` — i.e. all of `google/`, `anthropic/`, `openai/`, `meta-llama/`, etc. (the majority of OpenRouter's catalog).

## Versions

- `@mastra/core@^1.31.0`
- `@mastra/observability@^1.11.0`
- `@mastra/libsql@^1.9.1`
- Storage: DuckDB for observability domain (so metrics ARE stored).

## Repro

Minimal Mastra setup with one agent on an OpenRouter route:

```ts
const agent = new Agent({
  id: 'demo',
  name: 'demo',
  instructions: 'Return strict JSON.',
  model: 'openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-flash',
});

await agent.generate('What is 2+2? Return {"r":<num>}.', {
  structuredOutput: { schema: z.object({ r: z.number() }) },
});
```

Then inspect `metric_events`:

```sql
SELECT name, value, estimatedCost, costUnit, costMetadata
FROM metric_events
WHERE name = 'mastra_model_total_input_tokens'
ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1;
```

Result:

```
name= mastra_model_total_input_tokens
value= 27
estimatedCost= null
costUnit= null
costMetadata= {"error":"no_matching_model"}
```

## Root cause

What the `MODEL_GENERATION` span records:

```json
{
  "provider":     "openrouter",
  "model":        "google/gemini-2.5-flash",
  "responseModel":"google/gemini-2.5-flash"
}
```

What the bundled `pricing-data.jsonl` contains for the same model:

```json
{"i":"2b85a04d2eed9c48","p":"openrouter","m":"gemini-2-5-flash", ...}
```

In `node_modules/@mastra/observability/dist/index.js`, `getModelVariants(model)` produces:

```ts
[
  "google/gemini-2.5-flash",
  "google/gemini-2-5-flash",   // dot → dash
  "google/gemini-2.5-flash",   // stripDateSuffix(orig) — no-op
  "google/gemini-2-5-flash",   // stripDateSuffix(dashed) — no-op
]
```

None of these contain `gemini-2-5-flash` (without the `google/` prefix), so the lookup misses.

Verified by grep on the bundled registry — **0 of 410 `provider:"openrouter"` entries have a `vendor/` prefix in the model id**:

```
$ grep '"p":"openrouter"' pricing-data.jsonl | grep -c '"m":"google/'
0
$ grep -c '"p":"openrouter"' pricing-data.jsonl
410
```

## Suggested fix (one of)

1. **Pricing-side**: in `getModelVariants` (or `PricingRegistry.get`), additionally try `model.split('/').pop()` (strip leading vendor segment when the provider is a gateway like `openrouter`).
2. **Span-side**: when populating `attrs.model` for an OpenRouter call, store only the bare model id (`gemini-2.5-flash`), not the full route id.
3. **Registry-side**: ship duplicate openrouter entries with vendor prefix in `m`. Largest blast radius and ongoing maintenance, probably the worst option.

(1) feels cleanest — `provider === 'openrouter'` is already known at lookup time, and the current variants logic is the natural place to add a "strip leading segment" attempt as a fallback.

## Impact

- **Token metrics are emitted correctly** (good — that's how we noticed the costs were missing rather than silently zero'd).
- **Cost metrics fail open** (`estimatedCost: null`, `costMetadata.error: "no_matching_model"`) — Studio's "Total Model Cost" panel reads "No data yet" for any user routing through OpenRouter with a vendor prefix.

Happy to PR the variants-fix if it'd be useful.


### Steps To Reproduce

  1. Clone https://github.com/Egorles/mastra-cost-bug-repro
  2. cd mastra-cost-bug-repro && npm install
  3. echo 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...' > .env
  4. npm run repro

  Expected: estimatedCost is a number; costUnit is "USD".
  Actual:   estimatedCost is null; costUnit is null;
            costMetadata is {"error":"no_matching_model"}.

  The script:
    a) registers an Agent with model: 'openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-flash'
    b) calls agent.generate() with a tiny structuredOutput schema
    c) waits for the DefaultExporter to flush
    d) reads back the model_generation span and the
       mastra_model_total_input_tokens metric from mastra.duckdb,
       showing the span attrs (provider="openrouter",
       model="google/gemini-2.5-flash") and the missed registry lookup.

  Token metrics ARE populated correctly (value=20). Only cost fields
  are null because the registry only has bare model ids
  (provider="openrouter", m="gemini-2-5-flash") — none of the 410
  openrouter entries include a vendor/ prefix:

    $ grep '"p":"openrouter"' pricing-data.jsonl | grep -c '"m":"google/'
0

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://github.com/Egorles/mastra-cost-bug-repro

### Expected Behavior

estimatedCost is populated with a number, costUnit is "USD",
  and Studio's "Total Model Cost" / "Model Usage & Cost" panels
  show real $ values for OpenRouter routes that include a vendor
  prefix in the model id (e.g. openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-flash,
  openrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5).

  The registry already contains a matching entry for the same
  model under provider="openrouter", model="gemini-2-5-flash" —
  the lookup just needs to consider the variant where the leading
  vendor segment ("google/") is stripped from the span's model id
  before matching.

### Environment Information

```block
- @mastra/core:          1.31.0
  - @mastra/observability: 1.11.0
  - @mastra/libsql:        1.9.1
  - @mastra/duckdb:        1.2.0
  - zod:                   4.4.2
  - Node.js:               22.22.1
  - npm:                   (whatever ships with Node 22.22.1)
  - OS:                    macOS (Darwin 25.1.0, arm64)
  - Storage:               LibSQL (default) + DuckDB (observability domain)
                           via MastraCompositeStore
  - Exporter:              DefaultExporter (no external observability backend)
  - Model gateway:         OpenRouter
                           model = "openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-flash"
                           (any openrouter/<vendor>/<model> route reproduces
                            the same lookup miss)
```

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

title: [RFC] Runtime signals and trusted policy enforcement
body:
## Problem

When an app starts a Mastra run, the app often already knows some important runtime facts:

- this run came from a chat message, a UI button, a webhook, a schedule, or a retry
- only a specific capability should be available for this turn
- some tools should be hidden, some should require approval, and some should be blocked
- the same decision should apply to normal tools, dynamic tools, client/provider tools, and server-side execution

Mastra has the building blocks for this, but not one trusted place to store and enforce the decision.

## What Apps Have To Do Today

Today an app that needs this behavior has to build a userland policy system around Mastra:

- put a "turn contract" or policy object into public `RequestContext`
- add input processors that prune `tools`, `activeTools`, and `toolChoice`
- add prompt text telling the model which tools it may use
- add output processors that reject disallowed tool calls after the model emits them
- wrap `ToolSearchProcessor` so dynamic `search_tools` / `load_tool` cannot reveal blocked tools
- add parity tests so prompt text, tool-family maps, and real runtime tools do not drift
- handle durable resume/restart behavior separately

That workaround is reasonable for a production app, but it is fragile. The policy is scattered across request context, processors, prompts, dynamic-tool wrappers, and tests.

## Why This Is A Framework Gap

Some parts cannot be solved cleanly from normal userland processors:

- public `RequestContext` is mutable app/userland state, not a trusted internal policy boundary
- `requestContextSchema` validates `requestContext.all`, so internal framework policy should not live as normal context data
- `prepareStep` runs after normal input-step processors, so a normal processor cannot guarantee final tool narrowing
- dynamic tools, client tools, and provider-defined tools must be filtered before the model sees them
- server-side tool execution still needs a final rejection check
- approval required by runtime policy should not be downgraded by conditional tool approval
- tracing should show why a request was allowed, narrowed, blocked, or escalated

Related narrower issue: #16045 covers request-context-aware `ToolSearchProcessor` filtering. This issue is the broader parent problem.

## Proposed Direction

Add a small experimental runtime-policy layer:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Request trigger] --> B[Trusted runtime policy]
  B --> C[Final pre-model tool enforcement]
  C --> D[Model call]
  D --> E[Pre-tool rejection]
  E --> F[Tool execution]
```

Concretely:

- internal runtime-state carrier attached to `RequestContext`, hidden from `.all`, normal `toJSON()`, and public schema validation
- minimal `RuntimeSignals` / `RuntimePolicy` types
- app/framework-assigned trust for signal providers
- deterministic merge of accepted observations
- capability-to-runtime-tool-name resolution
- final pre-model enforcement after `prepareStep`
- pre-tool rejection before server-side execution
- `observe` mode first, so apps can trace would-deny/would-narrow decisions before enforcing

## Non-Goals For The First Cut

- no new router or workflow engine
- no mandatory migration for existing agents
- no universal natural-language classifier
- no full evidence or slot-filling system yet

## Success Criteria

- disabled by default
- apps can trace why tools were allowed or denied
- `prepareStep` or another processor cannot accidentally re-expose denied tools
- dynamic search/load cannot surface tools outside the active policy
- server-side tool calls outside policy are rejected

title: fix(server): emit Responses streaming events for tool calls
body:
## Problem

Mastra server `/v1/responses` streaming was text-first: agent stream chunks for tool calls and tool results were not translated into Responses-style server-sent events (SSE), even though completed and stored response output can represent `function_call` and `function_call_output` items.

That means clients reconstructing response state from streaming events can miss tool activity until `response.completed`, and stored fallback output can lose tool items when an agent stream does not provide DB messages.

Local references:

- `packages/server/src/server/schemas/responses.ts` models `function_call` and `function_call_output` output items.
- `packages/server/src/server/handlers/responses.adapter.ts` maps persisted Mastra tool messages into Responses output/conversation items.
- `packages/server/src/server/handlers/responses.ts` owns the Mastra-stream to Responses-SSE bridge.

## Task

Implement Responses-compatible SSE translation for Mastra server `/v1/responses` streaming so tool calls and tool results are represented as ordered Responses output items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Existing text streaming behavior stays compatible.
- Tool-call chunks emit ordered `response.output_item.added`, `response.function_call_arguments.delta`, `response.function_call_arguments.done`, and `response.output_item.done` events.
- Tool-result and tool-error chunks emit `function_call_output` output items when paired with a known tool call.
- Streamed events include `sequence_number` and otherwise follow the OpenAI Responses streaming event fields for the emitted event types.
- Final `response.completed.response.output` preserves streamed output item order when DB messages are unavailable.
- Stored fallback output can be retrieved and replayed without duplicating tool calls or losing text output.
- Client JS types include streamed function-call argument events.
- Tests cover text streaming, legacy v1 streams, streamed tool arguments, duplicate tool chunks, multiple tool calls, tool-only streams, zero-argument tools, tool errors, fallback storage/retrieval, and text-before-tool ordering.

## Out of Scope

- Azure/OpenAI provider routing.
- WebSocket transport, background mode, webhooks, reconnect recovery, or benchmarks.
- Reasoning output items. Mastra's current server Responses schema does not model a reasoning output item, so this issue stays scoped to tool-call-compatible output already represented by the schema.
- Hosted tools, multimodal output, and broad provider compatibility matrix work.

title: @mastra/langfuse: Anthropic generation spans report tokens=0 (LangfuseExporter native path, @mastra/core@1.31.0)
body:
## Summary

When using the native `LangfuseExporter` from `@mastra/langfuse@1.2.5` (latest) with `@mastra/core@1.31.0`, generation spans for Anthropic models arrive in Langfuse with `usage={input:0, output:0, total:0}`. The same setup with OpenAI models works correctly. This is the same class of issue as #8162 (closed without fix), #13848, and #15962 — but reproducing on the latest published versions, against a freshly self-hosted Langfuse v3 stack.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| `@mastra/core` | 1.31.0 |
| `@mastra/langfuse` | 1.2.5 (latest) |
| `@mastra/observability` | (transitive) |
| Langfuse server | self-hosted v3 (testing 3.42.0 → upgrading to 3.172.1) |
| Transport | OTLP HTTP via Langfuse OTel ingest endpoint |
| Runtime | Node 22, ECS Fargate ARM64 |
| Anthropic SDK | via Vercel AI SDK adapter |
| Streaming | yes (`agent.stream()`) |

## Reproduction

```ts
import { LangfuseExporter } from '@mastra/langfuse';

const exporter = new LangfuseExporter({
  publicKey: process.env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY,
  secretKey: process.env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY,
  baseUrl: process.env.LANGFUSE_HOST,
});

// Mastra config wires this exporter via observability.export.exporter
```

1. Run an agent step that calls Claude Opus 4 / Opus 4.7 / Opus 4.6 (any current Anthropic model) via the Vercel AI SDK Anthropic adapter.
2. Inspect the resulting Langfuse observation.

## Observed

Parent agent span (named `chat <model>`):

```json
{
  "name": "chat claude-opus-4-7",
  "model": "claude-opus-4-7",
  "usage": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "total": 0 },
  "inputPrice": null,
  "outputPrice": null,
  "calculatedTotalCost": null
}
```

The provider call definitely returned tokens (response was non-empty, content was generated). The same trace, when fronted by LiteLLM (which emits its own `litellm_request` child span via `langfuse_otel`), shows correct token counts on the LiteLLM-emitted child span. So the data exists at the AI SDK level — it's not making it through Mastra's span population for Anthropic.

OpenAI generation spans in the same trace structure do populate tokens correctly.

## Expected

`usage.input`, `usage.output`, and `usage.total` populated for Anthropic spans, matching the actual provider response.

## Likely cause

Anthropic's Vercel AI SDK adapter reports usage at `providerMetadata.anthropic.{inputTokens, outputTokens}` rather than on the OTel `gen_ai.usage.*` standard attributes. PR #13914 added a `providerMetadata` fallback for streaming finish chunks, fixing cache tokens specifically. The non-cache-token output count for Anthropic may still be missing — output tokens read from the wrong path or never populated on the generation span.

Related history:
- #8162 — original report (closed 2025-09 without a linked fix PR)
- #13848 / PR #13914 — addressed cache metrics in streaming
- #15962 — non-spec attribute names on `@mastra/otel-exporter` (closed 2026-04-30)
- langfuse/langfuse discussion [#8038](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8038) — Langfuse-side context

## Workaround in use today

Route through LiteLLM. The `langfuse_otel` callback emits a separate `litellm_request` child span that carries correct tokens. Trace-level cost aggregation in Langfuse sums child spans, so dashboards filtered by trace remain correct. Only the parent agent span visually shows 0.

## Impact

- Parent agent span tokens read 0 in the Langfuse UI for any Anthropic-only span
- Confuses span-level metrics filtered to a single span (vs trace aggregation)
- Affects auto-cost-computation when the parent span is the only one Langfuse can match against its model-pricing table

Happy to provide additional repro details or test a candidate fix against this stack.

title: [BUG] claude-opus-4-7 deprecates `temperature` — agent.stream() returns 400, no framework-level handling (parity with PrefillErrorHandler)
body:
### Describe the Bug

Anthropic's 2026 breaking change to `claude-opus-4-7` (and likely the wider 4.7 family) **deprecates the `temperature` parameter** (along with `top_p` / `top_k`). Any request that includes `temperature` returns:

```
400 — `temperature` is deprecated for this model.
```

Mastra's `agent.stream()` carries a default `temperature` (or whatever the user sets in `defaultOptions` / per-call `callSettings`) straight through to `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, which forwards it to the API verbatim. The result is a hard 400 in production with no graceful path.

This is the same shape of breaking change that motivated #13969 / #14435 (prefill removed in 4.5/4.6) — **a model in a previously-supported family quietly drops a parameter**, and the framework has no capability layer to absorb it.

#### Live failure

Production agent on `claude-opus-4-7` with `temperature: 0.3` → 400 mid-stream → run fails for the user with no automatic recovery. We currently have no way to ship 4-7 without forking Mastra or sanitising `callSettings` outside the framework.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a Mastra `Agent` configured with `model: anthropic('claude-opus-4-7')` and any non-zero `temperature` (or rely on the SDK default).
2. Call `agent.stream({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hello' }] })`.
3. Anthropic returns `400 'temperature' is deprecated for this model.`
4. The error surfaces to the user; there is no `processAPIError` hook that fires for this since the `PrefillErrorHandler` regex doesn't match, and no other built-in processor strips the param.

### Expected Behavior

Pick one of these (in order of preference):

1. **Auto-strip dropped-capability params** for known models. Same shape as the auto-injected `PrefillErrorHandler` — a built-in `inputProcessor` (or call-settings sanitiser) consults a capability matrix per `provider+modelId` and removes params the model doesn't accept (`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, prefill-trailing-assistant, etc.) before dispatch.
2. **Expose a public capability matrix users can extend.** e.g. `setModelCapabilities('claude-opus-4-7', { supportsTemperature: false })` so adding a new Anthropic / OpenAI / xAI release becomes a one-row catalog edit instead of a code search across every agent definition.
3. **At minimum: a built-in `TemperatureDeprecatedHandler`** sibling to `PrefillErrorHandler`, registered the same way (auto-injected via `errorProcessors`), that on the 400 strips `temperature` (and `top_p`/`top_k`) from `runState.callSettings` and signals retry.

### Why this matters / context

The ecosystem is hitting this same shape across frameworks each time Anthropic ships a breaking change:

- 4.5 / 4.6 prefill: #13969 (fixed via #14435 — auto-injected `PrefillErrorHandler`)
- 4.7 temperature: this issue
- LiteLLM has the same bug open: BerriAI/litellm#26444
- Roo-Code: RooCodeInc/Roo-Code#12162
- anything-llm: Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm#5461

Each framework currently solves it independently with its own per-model deny-list. Mastra is uniquely positioned to handle this at the `provider + processor` layer so users don't have to maintain their own `model_capabilities.ts`.

The `processAPIError` infrastructure that #14435 added is exactly the right primitive — it just needs (a) more matchers and (b) a way for the matcher to mutate `callSettings`, not just `messageList`. From the #14435 PR description, processors today can mutate `messageList` and signal `{ retry: true }`; if `processAPIError` were extended to allow mutating `callSettings` (or returning a patched options bag), a stock `TemperatureDeprecatedHandler` becomes ~20 lines.

### Reference

- #13969 — sibling issue (4.6 prefill, fixed in #14435)
- #14435 — `processAPIError` + auto-injected `PrefillErrorHandler` (the pattern to follow)
- BerriAI/litellm#26444 — same root cause in LiteLLM

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate (no issue mentions `claude-opus-4-7` + `temperature` as of filing).
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue.

title: Add lifecycle timestamps to Harness display state
body:
## Problem

Harness display state tracks active tool and subagent lifecycle status, but it does not expose when those lifecycle entries started or completed.

On current `main`:

- `ActiveToolState` has `status`, `result`, and related display fields, but no start or completion timestamp.
- `ActiveSubagentState` has `status` and terminal `durationMs`, but no `startedAt` / `completedAt` values.
- Harness already owns the event stream that creates, updates, completes, and errors these entries, so UI consumers should not need to maintain separate timing maps outside the framework.

## Proposed shape

Add timestamp fields to Harness display state entries:

- `ActiveToolState.startedAt?: Date`
- `ActiveToolState.completedAt?: Date`
- `ActiveSubagentState.startedAt?: Date`
- `ActiveSubagentState.completedAt?: Date`

Populate them inside Harness display-state updates:

- Set `startedAt` when a tool first enters `tool_input_start` or `tool_start`.
- Preserve the original `startedAt` when `tool_input_start` is followed by `tool_start` for the same `toolCallId`.
- Set `completedAt` when `tool_end` arrives.
- Set `completedAt` when `agent_end` forces an in-flight tool to `error`.
- Set `startedAt` on `subagent_start` and `completedAt` on `subagent_end`.

## Notes

This issue is intentionally scoped to the display state that exists on current `main`. Retained subagent history is not currently part of `HarnessDisplayState`; if that is added separately, any history-entry type that derives from `ActiveSubagentState` should naturally inherit these timestamp fields.

The AI SDK client package does not currently expose a Harness display-state snapshot path on `main`, so this issue should be verified in core Harness display-state tests rather than claiming an AI SDK harness serialization change.

## Acceptance criteria

- Active tool display state includes `startedAt` while streaming input or running.
- Completed and errored tool display state includes `completedAt`.
- Tools forced to `error` by `agent_end` include `completedAt`.
- Active subagent display state includes `startedAt` while running.
- Completed or errored subagent display state includes `completedAt`.
- Existing `status`, `durationMs`, and lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.
- Display-state subscriber snapshots clone timestamp values rather than sharing mutable `Date` instances with live state.
- Focused Harness display-state tests cover active and terminal timestamp behavior.

title: Batch DuckDB observability schema initialization
body:
## Problem

DuckDB observability initialization currently executes each DDL and additive migration with a separate `this.db.execute(...)` call.

Each `DuckDBConnection.execute()` call opens a DuckDB connection, runs one statement, and closes the connection. With all observability tables and additive migrations, startup performs many sequential connection/run/close cycles before the store can be used.

## Why not Promise.all

The original performance concern looks like an N+1 query issue, but parallelizing DDL/migrations with `Promise.all` would be risky:

- schema operations should remain ordered and deterministic
- migrations depend on tables existing first
- DuckDB DDL/write operations can contend on schema/writer locks
- parallel failures would be harder to diagnose

## Proposed fix

Add an ordered batch execution helper on `DuckDBConnection` for no-parameter schema setup statements. Use it from DuckDB observability `init()` to run `ALL_DDL` and `ALL_MIGRATIONS` through one DuckDB connection while preserving statement order.

## Acceptance criteria

- DuckDB observability init uses one ordered batch call for schema DDL and additive migrations.
- Migration order remains deterministic.
- Existing observability behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests cover the batch helper and observability init using it.

title: Add subagent display names to Harness display state
body:
## Problem

`HarnessSubagent` definitions already include a human-readable `name`, but Harness subagent display state only carries `agentType`. UI consumers that render active or completed delegation state have to repeat the `agentType -> name` lookup outside the framework.

That lookup belongs in Harness display state because Harness owns both the subagent configuration and the active state it emits.

## Proposed shape

Add optional `displayName?: string` to `ActiveSubagentState` and expose `HarnessSubagentHistoryEntry` as `Omit<ActiveSubagentState, "status">` for terminal display state consumers.

Populate `displayName` from the configured `HarnessSubagent.name` for the matching `agentType` when Harness creates subagent display entries.

## Acceptance criteria

- Active subagent display state includes `displayName` when the configured subagent has a matching `name`.
- Terminal subagent history entries preserve the same `displayName`.
- Existing `agentType` behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests cover active and terminal/history display state.

title: Bundled Studio routes bypass server.auth, including /refresh-events SSE
body:
## Bug description

When deploying Mastra with bundled Studio via `mastra build --studio`, API routes are protected by `server.auth`, but Studio routes are still publicly reachable.

Observed public routes in the bundled server:

- `GET /refresh-events`
- `POST /__refresh`
- `GET /__hot-reload-status`
- Studio static shell/assets

In the installed bundle, Studio opens the SSE stream with native `EventSource`:

```js
new EventSource(`${basePath}/refresh-events`)
```

The corresponding server handler does not appear to check `server.auth`, cookies, `Authorization`, or query tokens before creating the SSE stream. It also returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

## Expected behavior

If Studio is bundled into the same deployed API server and `server.auth` is configured, Studio routes should either:

1. be protected by the same auth provider,
2. support a documented Studio auth/session mechanism for SSE and hot-reload routes, or
3. clearly document that bundled Studio routes are intentionally public and must be protected by an external proxy.

Because native browser `EventSource` cannot send a custom Bearer `Authorization` header, a fix likely needs cookie/session auth or another documented token mechanism for the Studio SSE connection.

## Actual behavior

`server.auth` protects API routes, but bundled Studio routes appear to be mounted outside that auth boundary.

## Why this matters

A production deployment can unintentionally expose Mastra Studio/hot-reload endpoints even though the API server itself requires authentication.

## Environment

- `mastra`: `1.5.0`
- `@mastra/core`: `1.24.1`
- `@mastra/server`: `1.24.1`
- `@mastra/deployer`: `1.24.1`
- build command: `mastra build --studio`

## Related issues

This seems related to, but not exactly covered by, existing Studio auth issues such as #13794, #13901, #14769, #15470, and #15910.

title: [BUG] @mastra/pg: agent listing crashes when model is stored as jsonb scalar string (one bad row breaks entire endpoint)
body:
## Summary

`@mastra/pg`'s `parseJson` in agent listing endpoints crashes with **HTTP 500** when any row in `mastra_agent_versions.model` is stored as a **JSONB scalar string** (e.g. `"google/gemini-3-flash"`). One bad row breaks the entire listing for all agents (fail-fast).

## Environment

- `@mastra/pg`: 1.9.1
- `@mastra/core`: ^1.24.1
- Postgres: Neon (jsonb columns)
- Driver: `pg` (default behavior auto-parses jsonb)

## Reproduction

1. Create an agent version where `model` is written as a JSON scalar string. This can happen via `createVersion({ model: "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5" })` because `createVersion` does `JSON.stringify(input.model)` without normalizing scalar inputs to objects (see `dist/index.js:3995`).
2. The DB ends up with `jsonb_typeof(model) = 'string'`.
3. Call any endpoint that lists agents (e.g. the Mastra Editor's `/api/stored/agents?status=published`).
4. Response:

```
HTTP/2 500
{"error":"Failed to parse JSON for field \"model\": Unexpected token 'g', \"google/gem\"... is not valid JSON"}
```

## Root cause

Two problems compound:

### 1. Double-deserialization in `parseJson` (read path)

`dist/index.js:3690`:

```js
parseJson(value, fieldName) {
  if (!value) return void 0;
  if (typeof value !== "string") return value;
  try { return JSON.parse(value); } catch (error) { ... throw }
}
```

For a `jsonb` column, the `pg` driver already deserializes the value:

| DB value (jsonb)                  | Driver returns (JS)                      |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `{"name":"x","provider":"y"}`     | `{ name: "x", provider: "y" }` (object)  |
| `"google/gemini-3-flash"`         | `"google/gemini-3-flash"` (**JS string**) |

For the second case, `parseJson` sees `typeof === "string"` and runs `JSON.parse("google/gemini-3-flash")` — which throws on the unquoted `g`.

`parseJson` cannot distinguish "string containing JSON" (text column) from "JSON scalar string already deserialized" (jsonb column).

### 2. Fail-fast in `mapAgentRow` (listing endpoint)

`dist/index.js:4237`:

```js
model: this.parseJson(row.model, "model"),
```

`mapAgentRow` runs synchronously over every row in the listing. One row that throws kills the entire endpoint, hiding **all** agents from the Editor — even ones with valid `model`.

### 3. Asymmetric write path

`createVersion` (`dist/index.js:3995`) does:

```js
JSON.stringify(input.model)
```

with no type validation. Passing `input.model = "slug"` is silently accepted and stored as a jsonb scalar string, guaranteeing the read path will later fail.

## Impact

In our deployment, **9 of 21 agents** had model stored as scalar string (a mix of historical UPDATEs and edits via the Mastra Editor). The result was a fully broken Editor listing in production. Worked around with:

```sql
UPDATE mastra_agent_versions
SET model = jsonb_build_object('slug', model #>> '{}')
WHERE jsonb_typeof(model) = 'string';
```

Runtime kept working only because we have a custom override layer that tolerates scalar strings; the Editor was the only consumer that crashed.

## Suggested fixes

1. **`parseJson`**: when the storage column type is known to be `jsonb` (which is the case for `model`, `tools`, `defaultOptions`, etc.), skip `JSON.parse` and return the driver-provided value as-is. Reserve `JSON.parse` for `text`-typed columns.
2. **Listing endpoints**: don't fail-fast. If a row fails to parse, log + skip + return the rest. A single bad row shouldn't take down the whole UI.
3. **`createVersion` (write path)**: normalize string inputs to a consistent shape (e.g. `{ slug: input.model }`) or reject with a typed error. Symmetric write/read.

Happy to send a PR if there's interest in any of the three.

## Affected callers (in our codebase)

```
node_modules/@mastra/pg/dist/index.js:4237   // mapAgentRow → parseJson(row.model)
node_modules/@mastra/pg/dist/index.js:3995   // createVersion → JSON.stringify(input.model)
node_modules/@mastra/pg/dist/index.js:3690   // parseJson definition
```

title: [BUG] Mastra Studio: Enum dropdown does not persist selection
body:
### Describe the Bug

What GPT gave me:

I reproduced it locally. It’s almost certainly **upstream in Mastra Studio**, not React Flow or your workflow code.

What I saw:

- `selection.mode` is defined correctly as a Zod enum in types.ts.
- Studio renders it as a combobox.
- The dropdown opens and the options are clickable.
- Clicking `explicit` closes the menu, but the value stays `needs-og-published`.

So the click reaches the option, but Studio’s generated form state does not apply the enum change. That’s a Mastra Studio form-renderer bug.

You can work around it here in two ways:

1. Use the **JSON** tab instead of Form mode.
2. Change `mode` locally from `z.enum(...)` to `z.string().default(...)`, then validate it manually in `parseWorkflowInput`. That would make Studio render a text input instead of the broken enum dropdown. Not as nice, but usable.

A real dropdown fix should happen upstream in Mastra Studio. This repo can only sidestep it.

### Steps To Reproduce

Minimal repro:

```ts
// src/mastra/index.ts
import { Mastra } from '@mastra/core/mastra'
import { createWorkflow, createStep } from '@mastra/core/workflows'
import { z } from 'zod'

const InputSchema = z.object({
  mode: z.enum(['a', 'b']).default('a'),
})

const step = createStep({
  id: 'step',
  inputSchema: InputSchema,
  outputSchema: z.object({ mode: z.string() }),
  execute: async ({ inputData }) => inputData,
})

const workflow = createWorkflow({
  id: 'enumDropdownBug',
  inputSchema: InputSchema,
  outputSchema: z.object({ mode: z.string() }),
})
  .then(step)
  .commit()

export const mastra = new Mastra({
  workflows: { enumDropdownBug: workflow },
})
```

```json
// package.json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "mastra dev"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@mastra/core": "^1.32.1",
    "mastra": "^1.8.1",
    "zod": "^4.4.3"
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash
bun install
bun run dev
```

Open:

```text
http://localhost:4111/workflows/enumDropdownBug/graph
```

Repro steps:

1. Open **Current Run**.
2. In Form mode, click `mode`.
3. Select `b`.
4. Dropdown closes, but value stays `a`.

Expected: value changes to `b`.

Actual: option click is received, but selected enum value reverts/stays at default.

[bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27408439/bug.zip)

Enum selector should be clickable.

```block
Mac M4 using Ghostty Terminal with Zellij & Fish Shell.
```

title: Expose declined HITL tool approvals as denied UI stream chunks
body:
## Problem

Current `main` does not expose declined HITL tool approvals as a first-class AI SDK v5 UI stream chunk.

The current AI SDK v5 stream adapter is `convertFullStreamChunkToUIMessageStream`. It maps generic `tool-error` chunks to `tool-output-error`, but there is no corresponding semantic `tool-output-denied` chunk for the approval-decline path.

Some approval-denial paths currently encode denial as a normal tool result string such as `Tool call was not approved by the user`, while Harness display state marks terminal tool errors generically as `error`. Consumers that need to distinguish "the user declined this tool" from "the tool failed" should not have to infer that from localized/free-form text.

## Proposed shape

Add a native AI SDK v5 UI stream chunk shape for declined tool approvals:

```ts
{ type: "tool-output-denied"; toolCallId: string; reason?: string }
```

Preserve denial as semantic state before it reaches the UI stream adapter. This can be represented as a terminal Harness tool state such as `denied`, or an equivalent display/stream state that lets the adapter emit `tool-output-denied` without string matching.

## Acceptance criteria

- Declined tool approvals can produce `tool-output-denied` from the AI SDK v5 UI stream adapter.
- Ordinary tool execution failures continue to produce `tool-output-error`.
- The adapter does not infer denial by matching localized/free-form error or result text.
- Tests cover both declined approval and generic tool failure.

title: [BUG] Cost estimation misses OpenRouter models — pricing lookup doesn't handle "vendor/model" ids
body:
## Describe the Bug

Cost is `—` for OpenRouter models in observability/metrics. Token columns populate, cost doesn't.

OpenRouter reports model ids as `vendor/model` (e.g. `openai/gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07`, `xiaomi/mimo-v2-pro-20260318`). The pricing JSONL stores `provider:"openrouter"` rows under two different conventions:

- slash flattened to dash, vendor prefix kept: `xiaomi-mimo-v2-pro`, `meta-llama-llama-3-1-405b`
- vendor prefix dropped entirely: `gpt-5-mini`, `claude-3-5-sonnet`

`getModelVariants()` in `observability/mastra/src/metrics/pricing-registry.ts` handles `.` → `-` (#14959) and date suffixes (#15349), but not `/`, so neither stored form is ever reached.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Run an agent against any OpenRouter model.
2. Open the observability **Model Usage & Cost** panel.

Observed:

```
openai/gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07     222    320     0   0   —
xiaomi/mimo-v2-pro-20260318    129.1K  3.2K  63.6K  0   —
```

## Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

N/A — reproducible directly against the shipped `pricing-data.jsonl` using the variant logic in `pricing-registry.ts:199-202`. Happy to provide a failing unit test (and have a fix ready as a follow-up PR).

## Expected Behavior

Cost resolves. `getModelVariants()` should additionally try `model.replace(/[./]/g, '-')` and `model.substring(model.indexOf('/') + 1)`, with `stripDateSuffix` applied to each.

## Environment Information

- Package: `@mastra/observability` (current `main`)
- LLM Provider: OpenRouter (any `vendor/model` id)
- Not env-dependent — pure pricing-data lookup mismatch.

title: [BUG] SemanticRecall can produce orphan tool_use/tool_result blocks (Anthropic 400)
body:
## Describe the Bug

`SemanticRecall` can inject historical messages into the prompt that produce orphan `tool_use` / `tool_result` blocks when the messages are converted to provider format. With Anthropic this is fatal — Anthropic rejects the request with `messages.N.content.0: unexpected tool_use_id found in tool_result blocks ... Each tool_result block must have a corresponding tool_use block in the previous message.` and the agent turn fails before any output is produced.

This bites hardest in three combinations that are individually reasonable:

1. `semanticRecall.scope: "resource"` (cross-thread recall)
2. `semanticRecall.messageRange` is small (we hit it on `2`, the doc default is `1`)
3. The agent uses parallel tool calls (one assistant turn emits multiple `tool_use` blocks)

The reason this is invisible on OpenAI is that OpenAI's chat completions format tolerates orphan `tool` messages with mismatched `tool_call_id`s. Anthropic strictly enforces tool_use ↔ tool_result pairing in immediately adjacent messages, so the same message list is fine for one provider and fatal for the other.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create an agent with:
   ```ts
   const memory = new Memory({
     storage: new PostgresStore({ ... }),
     vector: new PgVector({ ... }),
     embedder,
     options: {
       lastMessages: 30,
       semanticRecall: { topK: 3, messageRange: 2, scope: "resource" },
     },
   })
   ```
2. Drive a conversation that produces parallel tool calls (e.g. two `web_fetch` calls in one assistant step). Have the run end / stream abort after only one of the two `tool_result`s is persisted (this is realistic — provider timeouts, cancellations, abandoned runs).
3. From a *different* thread for the same `resource`, send a fresh user message that vector-matches the earlier turn.
4. Anthropic rejects the request:

```
AI_APICallError: messages.20.content.0: unexpected `tool_use_id` found in `tool_result` blocks: <id>.
Each `tool_result` block must have a corresponding `tool_use` block in the previous message.
statusCode: 400
```

## Expected Behavior

`SemanticRecall` should never produce a prompt that violates the target provider's tool-pairing invariant. Either:

- expand the recall window to include the matching `tool_use` / `tool_result`, or
- drop orphans (tool-invocation parts in `state: 'call' | 'partial-call' | 'approval-requested' | 'approval-responded'`, plus any tool-invocation result with no matching tool_use earlier in the message list), or
- reformat orphan exchanges into text summaries

before returning the assembled `MessageList` to the agent.

## Root Cause (from reading the source)

In `@mastra/pg`'s `_getIncludedMessages`, window expansion around each match is purely temporal:

- Vector search picks `topK` matches.
- For each match, fetch `messageRange.before` rows where `createdAt <=` the match and `messageRange.after` rows where `createdAt >`.
- Deduplicate, sort by `createdAt`, return.

There is no step that checks "is this `tool_result`'s matching `tool_use` in the result set?" The same is true at the `SemanticRecall.processInput` level — `chunk-53NCBZKI.js`'s `performSemanticSearch` and the assembly that follows do not validate or enforce tool-pairing atomicity before the messages reach the LLM.

`MastraDBMessage` (V2) parts *are* atomic per part for tool-invocation `state: 'result'` — both `tool_use` and `tool_result` come from the same part. But:

- A part with `state: 'call' | 'partial-call' | 'approval-requested'` (call without result) materializes only the `tool_use` side.
- When same-thread expansion's window slices through a multi-message turn and only catches some of a parallel tool-call group, the survivors materialize as orphans on either side.
- When `lastMessages` brings in a tail of one thread and SemanticRecall layers same-resource matches from another thread on top, the assembled list can contain inconsistent tool exchanges.

`filterIncompleteToolCalls` (memory/types) and `MessageHistory.processOutputResult` only operate on the *current* turn / output persistence, not on recalled history. `ProviderHistoryCompat` rewrites tool IDs *reactively after* an API error, but doesn't address pairing.

This is consistent with the (closed) reports #3448 (Anthropic + Postgres memory order) and Discord #9311 ("Memory processors run on messages retrieved from storage via `memory.query()`, which happens BEFORE semantic recall embeddings are added to system messages").

## Proposed Fix

In `SemanticRecall.processInput` (or in a shared helper invoked by all memory input processors), after the messages have been assembled and before returning the `MessageList`, run a tool-pair sanitizer:

```ts
function sanitizeToolPairs(messages: MastraDBMessage[]): {
  messages: MastraDBMessage[]
  dropped: Array<{ toolCallId: string; reason: string }>
} {
  const seen = new Set<string>()
  const dropped: Array<{ toolCallId: string; reason: string }> = []
  const cleaned: MastraDBMessage[] = []

  for (const message of messages) {
    const parts = message.content?.parts ?? []
    const filtered = parts.filter(part => {
      if (part.type !== 'tool-invocation') return true
      const { toolCallId, state } = part.toolInvocation
      if (state === 'partial-call' || state === 'call' ||
          state === 'approval-requested' || state === 'approval-responded') {
        dropped.push({ toolCallId, reason: 'incomplete-state' })
        return false
      }
      if (seen.has(toolCallId)) {
        dropped.push({ toolCallId, reason: 'duplicate' })
        return false
      }
      seen.add(toolCallId)
      return true
    })
    if (filtered.length === 0) continue
    cleaned.push(filtered === parts ? message : { ...message, content: { ...message.content, parts: filtered } })
  }
  return { messages: cleaned, dropped }
}
```

A more thorough fix would, before dropping, attempt to *expand the window* so the missing pair member is included — that preserves more context. Either approach is strictly safer than the current behavior.

I'd be happy to send a PR. We've shipped the same logic locally as an `inputProcessor` registered after memory's processors; happy to upstream it.

## Environment Information

- `@mastra/core@1.31.0`
- `@mastra/memory@1.17.4`
- `@mastra/pg@1.9.4`
- LLM Provider: Anthropic via OpenRouter
- Node 22, Postgres 16

## Component

Memory / SemanticRecall

## Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate (the closest are #3448 — different cause, similar symptom — and Discord-sourced #9311 — about cleaning recalled content).
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue.

title: CLI lint should not execute next.config.js while checking serverExternalPackages
body:
## Problem

The CLI Next.js lint rule currently parses `next.config.js` by extracting the `nextConfig` object with a regex and evaluating it with `eval()`.

Affected file:

`packages/cli/src/commands/lint/rules/nextConfigRule.ts`

Current behavior:

```ts
const configMatch = nextConfigContent.match(/const nextConfig = ({[\s\S]*?});/);
if (!configMatch?.[1]) {
  return null;
}
const configStr = configMatch[1].replace(/\n/g, "").replace(/\s+/g, " ");
return eval(`(${configStr})`);
```

Because `next.config.js` belongs to the project being linted, this lets project-controlled JavaScript run inside the Mastra CLI process.

## Impact

This is a real code execution issue in the CLI lint path. A malicious or compromised project can execute arbitrary Node.js code when a developer or CI job runs the Mastra lint command.

Potential impact includes reading local files, reading environment variables, accessing CI secrets available to the process, or modifying files in the workspace.

This is not remote unauthenticated execution. Exploitation requires running the CLI lint command against a malicious or compromised project config. The severity is still high for developer and CI environments because the executed code inherits the lint process permissions.

## Expected behavior

The lint rule should inspect `serverExternalPackages` without executing any code from `next.config.js`.

## Suggested fix

Use static parsing for `next.config.js` and only read supported literal config shapes, for example:

- `const nextConfig = { serverExternalPackages: ["@mastra/*"] }`
- `module.exports = { serverExternalPackages: ["@mastra/*"] }`
- `export default { serverExternalPackages: ["@mastra/*"] }`

The parser should reject or ignore dynamic expressions instead of evaluating them.

## Acceptance criteria

- Remove `eval()` from the Next.js config lint rule.
- Preserve lint behavior for simple literal `serverExternalPackages` configs.
- Add a regression test proving code embedded in `next.config.js` is not executed during linting.
- Add a changeset for the CLI package.

title: [BUG] autoResumeSuspendedTools breaks memory and Gemini tool schema conversion with Zod 3/4
body:
## Describe the Bug

`autoResumeSuspendedTools: true` currently breaks agents that use normal tools and working memory with Google/Gemini models because Mastra mutates tool input schemas with resume fields in a way that is not schema-version safe.

This shows up in two related ways:

1. With `zod@3.25.76`, `@mastra/memory` vnext working memory fails when the agent calls the built-in `updateWorkingMemory` tool:

```text
TypeError: keyValidator._parse is not a function
```

2. With `zod@4.4.3`, the same agent fails earlier during tool preparation for a Google/Gemini model:

```text
Error executing step workflow.execution-workflow.step.prepare-tools-step: Error: [toJSONSchema]: Non-representable type encountered: optional
MastraError: [toJSONSchema]: Non-representable type encountered: optional
id: AGENT_GENERATE_FAILED
```

This seems serious because `autoResumeSuspendedTools` is the documented way to let an agent continue suspended workflow tools from the next user message, but enabling it globally also affects normal tools and internal memory tools. Disabling it avoids the memory failure, but then suspended workflow tools no longer resume naturally and can be restarted instead.

The root cause appears to be in the tool builder:

```ts
const isResumableTool =
  input.autoResumeSuspendedTools ||
  this.originalTool.id?.startsWith("agent-") ||
  this.originalTool.id?.startsWith("workflow-");

// ...
nextSchema = nextSchema.extend({
  suspendedToolRunId: z.string().describe("The runId of the suspended tool").nullable().optional(),
  resumeData: z.any().describe("The resumeData object created from the resumeSchema of suspended tool").optional(),
});
```

In the Zod 3 case, a Zod 3 object can be extended with fields from `zod/v4`. Zod 3 later tries to call `_parse` on Zod 4 child schemas, which matches the known v3/v4 mismatch pattern from #14347 / #14412.

In the Zod 4 case, tool preparation for Gemini/Google runs the mutated tool schemas through the Google schema compatibility path and fails on optional fields injected for autoresume. I verified this by calling Mastra's real `makeCoreTool(..., autoResumeSuspendedTools: true)` path: almost every tool with optional input fields failed with `[toJSONSchema]: Non-representable type encountered: optional`; a simple tool without optional fields passed.

## Steps To Reproduce

Minimal shape:

1. Create a Mastra project with:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@ai-sdk/google": "^3.0.67",
    "@mastra/core": "^1.31.0",
    "@mastra/memory": "^1.17.4",
    "@mastra/pg": "^1.9.4",
    "ai": "^6.0.174",
    "zod": "^3.25.76"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "mastra": "^1.7.3",
    "tsx": "^4.21.0",
    "typescript": "^6.0.3",
    "vitest": "^4.1.5"
  }
}
```

2. Define an agent using a Google/Gemini model, vnext working memory, a normal tool with optional fields, and `autoResumeSuspendedTools: true`:

```ts
import { Agent } from "@mastra/core/agent";
import { createTool } from "@mastra/core/tools";
import { Memory } from "@mastra/memory";
import { z } from "zod";

const exampleTool = createTool({
  id: "example-tool",
  description: "Example tool with optional input",
  inputSchema: z.object({
    query: z.string().min(1),
    limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(25).optional(),
  }),
  execute: async ({ context }) => ({ ok: true, context }),
});

export const agent = new Agent({
  id: "repro-agent",
  name: "Repro Agent",
  model: "google/gemini-3-flash-preview",
  defaultOptions: {
    autoResumeSuspendedTools: true,
  },
  tools: { exampleTool },
  memory: new Memory({
    options: {
      lastMessages: 10,
      workingMemory: {
        enabled: true,
        scope: "thread",
        version: "vnext",
        template: "# Working memory",
      },
    },
  }),
});
```

3. Run an agent call that causes working memory to update:

```ts
await agent.generate("Remember that my preferred name is Gorkis.", {
  memory: {
    thread: "repro-thread",
    resource: "repro-resource",
  },
  maxSteps: 4,
});
```

4. Observe `updateWorkingMemory` failing with:

```text
TypeError: keyValidator._parse is not a function
```

5. Change only `zod` to `^4.4.3` using a normal install, no `--force`, no `--legacy-peer-deps`.

6. Run the same agent call again.

7. Observe the agent fail before model execution while preparing tools:

```text
Error executing step workflow.execution-workflow.step.prepare-tools-step:
Error: [toJSONSchema]: Non-representable type encountered: optional
```

Additional validation from my app:

- Direct execution of the raw memory tool succeeds.
- Full `agent.generate(...)` with `autoResumeSuspendedTools: false` succeeds and persists working memory.
- Full `agent.generate(...)` with `autoResumeSuspendedTools: true` fails.
- Normal `npm install zod@^4 --workspace=apps/api` succeeds.
- Tests and build pass with Zod 4.
- The actual agent path still fails with Zod 4 during Google/Gemini tool preparation.

## Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

I do not have a public repo link yet, but the self-contained reproduction above is the minimal shape. If needed I can publish a tiny repo with only the agent, one optional-field tool, and the memory config.

## Expected Behavior

`autoResumeSuspendedTools: true` should not break normal tools or internal memory tools.

Expected behavior would be one of:

- Only agent/workflow tools are made resumable unless explicitly opted in.
- Or all tool schemas are converted to a schema representation that can safely accept `suspendedToolRunId` and `resumeData` without mixing Zod 3 and Zod 4 internals.
- Or the injected autoresume fields are added in a provider-compatible way before Google/Gemini JSON Schema conversion.

Working memory should be able to update successfully while workflow tools remain resumable.

## Environment Information

```block
System:
  OS: macOS 26.3.1
  CPU: (8) arm64 Apple M2
  Memory: 157.95 MB / 16.00 GB
  Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh
Binaries:
  Node: 25.5.0 - /opt/homebrew/bin/node
  npm: 11.13.0 - /opt/homebrew/bin/npm
  bun: 1.3.6 - /Users/gorkamagana/.bun/bin/bun
  Deno: 2.6.10 - /opt/homebrew/bin/deno
  Watchman: 2026.01.12.00 - /opt/homebrew/bin/watchman
Browsers:
  Brave Browser: 147.1.89.143
  Chrome: 147.0.7727.138
  Firefox: 148.0
  Safari: 26.3.1
npmGlobalPackages:
  @dotenvx/dotenvx: 1.51.1
  @google/gemini-cli: 0.37.1
  @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent: 0.66.0
  @openai/codex: 0.128.0
  eas-cli: 16.28.0
  ios-deploy: 1.12.2
  localtunnel: 2.0.2
  npm: 11.13.0

LLM Provider: Google Gemini
Model: google/gemini-3-flash-preview

Package versions:
  @mastra/core: 1.31.0
  @mastra/memory: 1.17.4
  @mastra/schema-compat: 1.2.9
  @mastra/pg: 1.9.4
  mastra: 1.7.3
  ai: 6.0.174
  @ai-sdk/google: 3.0.67
  zod: 3.25.76 and also reproduced a separate failure mode with 4.4.3
  typescript: 6.0.3
  vitest: 4.1.5
```

## Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue.

Related issues/PRs:

- #14347 describes the same `keyValidator._parse is not a function` failure pattern from mixed Zod 3/v4 schemas.
- #14412 describes the root cause as Zod v4 schemas wrapped with Zod v3 producing mixed schemas that crash because Zod 3 calls `_parse` on Zod 4 children.
- #14054 is related to `autoResumeSuspendedTools` behavior for workflow tools, but does not appear to cover this schema injection failure for normal tools and memory tools.

title: updateToolInvocation warning when using suspend/resume in harnesses
body:
This issue was created from Discord post 1500826529813499995:

[![Open in Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open_in_Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/channels/1309558646228779139/1500826529813499995)

**Problem**: whenever a tool call is suspended within the runtime of a harness, it does a call to the store/DB to sync/update the message list. When it is resumed, it does not check whether that DB/store call has finished, resulting in the warning in updateToolInvocation.

**This occurs/can be reproduced by** using a less instant store with a harness (so not SQLite, but for example: a hosted postgres instance), then in a tool: suspend and have a script auto-resume it.
In our case this happens because I wrote a custom harnessRoute that makes the harness fully AI SDK useChat compatible, and some tool calls that suspend can be auto-resumed because the frontend client has all information needed to auto-resume. Whenever that happens, the tool cannot by found in the message list by toolCallId, and the tool call result is dropped, breaking everything basically.

**My hypothesized easy fix would probably be** to update Harness.handleToolResume to check in the store whether the `snapshot.status` is `suspended`, and keep waiting until the status is indeed `suspended`, in which case it makes sense to actually resume a.tool call. It would add a round-trip to the store, but I think that is manageable because tool resuming does not happen a lot.

title: Retrieve Studio serialization mode from request context
body:
## Problem

`GET /agents/:agentId` already receives `requestContext`, and `formatAgent` already has Studio-specific serialization behavior. The route currently hard-codes `isStudio` to `false`, which leaves that behavior unreachable from this handler even when the request context identifies the request as coming from Studio.

## Impact

The TODO makes the handler harder to reason about because the serialization mode is disconnected from the context already available in the handler. It also means dynamic agent serialization cannot use the Studio placeholder behavior for missing request-context values through this endpoint.

This is a code-health and correctness cleanup, not a performance optimization.

## Desired change

Read a strict boolean Studio flag from `requestContext` and pass it to `formatAgent`. Preserve existing behavior when the flag is missing or not exactly `true`.

## Edge cases

- Missing `isStudio` should behave like the current route and serialize as non-Studio.
- `isStudio: true` should enable the existing placeholder request-context proxy.
- Non-boolean values such as `"true"` or `1` should not enable Studio mode.
- Existing version selection behavior through `status`, `versionId`, and request context should remain unchanged.

## Verification target

Add focused handler coverage for the Studio flag path and non-true edge cases, then run the package-scoped server tests, lint, and build.

title: [FEATURE] EU-hosted Mastra Cloud option for enterprise
body:
### Problem Statement

Mastra Cloud is currently hosted solely in the US. For teams based in the European Union, US‑only hosting is a non‑starter – many customers for SaaS require that all personal data stay within EU borders. And in the case of customer law, certified companies have to clearly state data processing happens outside the EU and it can hurt customer trust quite a bit.

### Proposed Solution

- Offer a Mastra Cloud region hosted entirely in the European Union (e.g., in Ireland, Germany or through an EU sovereign‑cloud provider). This region should ensure that:
- All data (threads, messages, workflow snapshots, logs and traces) are stored and processed within EU‑based data centres under EU jurisdiction.
- Backups remain in the EU, so there is no cross‑border data transfer.
- Depending on where Mastra Cloud is hosted, multiple regions in EU long-term would of course be great, but for now I believe just one region in EU would suffice. Round-trip-time is not necessarily what people are optimizing for with AI applications.

### Component

Other

### Alternatives Considered

Self‑hosting is an option and it is what we are doing currently in production.

### Example Use Case

In our case, we are a company that provides financial services to people. This means we are directly working with the consumer-law part of GDPR and other EU rules. For us, having an EU region for Mastra Cloud would very likely make us deploy on Mastra Cloud.

### Additional Context

I am open to provide more information on this if necessary. Discord username: _Vulcano_

in agent.ts:

Request context is passed as an option, but the userId arg is already separate by then.

title: [BUG] NestJS adapter coerces query values before schema validation unlike other adapters
body:
## Describe the bug

The NestJS adapter currently performs controller-level, schema-agnostic query value coercion before route schema validation.

This differs from the other server adapters. Express/Fastify/Hono/Koa normalize the framework query object and then rely on the shared route query parsing path. That shared path can JSON-parse values when the route `queryParamSchema` expects complex query fields such as objects, arrays, or records, but it does not blindly coerce every JSON-looking or scalar-looking string before schema validation.

In NestJS, query values are coerced before the route schema gets to decide the intended type. This means a route that explicitly declares a string query field can fail validation because NestJS converts the raw string before the schema can validate it. For routes without query schema validation, handlers may receive coerced values instead of raw query strings.

PR #16113 addresses one part of this by preserving numeric-looking query identifiers as strings, but NestJS still currently coerces:

- `"true"` -> `true`
- `"false"` -> `false`
- `"null"` -> `null`
- `'{"a":1}'` -> `{ a: 1 }`
- `"[1,2]"` -> `[1, 2]`

## Reproduction

Define a route with a string query parameter:

```ts
queryParamSchema: z.object({
  filter: z.string().optional(),
})
```

Send:

```http
GET /api/example?filter={"a":1}
```

## Expected behavior

For parity with Hono/Express/Fastify/Koa, the schema should receive and accept:

```ts
filter === '{"a":1}'
```

Because the route schema says `filter` is a string.

Schema-guided JSON parsing should only happen when the route schema expects a complex query field, for example `z.object(...)`, `z.array(...)`, or `z.record(...)`.

## Actual behavior

With the NestJS adapter, `filter` is JSON-parsed to `{ a: 1 }` before schema validation. Since the schema declares `filter` as `z.string()`, validation fails instead of accepting the raw query string.

For routes without a `queryParamSchema`, the handler may receive the coerced value directly.

## Cross-adapter behavior

This table is about **adapter pre-schema coercion**, not whether the shared route schema parser may later parse a value because the schema expects a complex query field.

| Request query | Intended schema example | Hono/Express/Fastify/Koa adapter pre-schema behavior | NestJS current behavior | Expected NestJS behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `?flag=true` | `z.string().optional()` or schema decides | `"true"` | `true` before validation | `"true"` |
| `?flag=false` | `z.string().optional()` or schema decides | `"false"` | `false` before validation | `"false"` |
| `?value=null` | `z.string().optional()` or schema decides | `"null"` | `null` before validation | `"null"` |
| `?filter={"a":1}` | `z.string().optional()` | `'{"a":1}'` | `{ a: 1 }` before validation, causing `z.string()` to fail | `'{"a":1}'` |
| `?items=[1,2]` | `z.string().optional()` or schema decides | `"[1,2]"` | `[1, 2]` before validation | `"[1,2]"` |
| `?id=123` | `z.string().optional()` | `"123"` | previously `123`; addressed by #16113 | `"123"` |

## Why this matters

Query strings are strings at the HTTP boundary. Mastra route schemas should control whether and how those strings are parsed or coerced.

Blind adapter-level coercion causes surprising validation behavior and breaks adapter parity. For example, a user may intentionally declare `z.string()` because they want to receive raw JSON text, IDs, flags, or other string-like values exactly as sent.

## Recommended fix

- Remove NestJS controller-level blind query value coercion.
- Keep `normalizeQueryParams()`.
- Let shared route schema parsing decide whether to parse/coerce query values.
- Users who want coercion should opt in via schema-level tools such as:
  - `z.coerce.boolean()`
  - `z.coerce.number()`
  - JSON-specific query helpers / preprocessors for fields that are intended to be objects or arrays.

Related PR: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/16113

title: [BUG] Scheduled workflows and NestJS routes mishandle prefixes and query IDs
body:
Scheduled workflows and the NestJS adapter have a few related request-path correctness issues that should be tracked separately from observability work.

Problems:
- Importing createWorkflow from @mastra/core/workflows and declaring schedule can fail because the public barrel does not load the evented workflow registration side effect.
- In @mastra/nestjs, a configured prefix such as /api is not enforced when matching Mastra routes, so unprefixed requests like /agents can still be handled by Mastra.
- The NestJS adapter coerces numeric-looking query values to numbers before route schema validation, which can reject or change string identifiers such as resourceId=123 or runId=123.

Expected behavior:
- The public @mastra/core/workflows entry point should support scheduled workflow promotion without a separate evented import.
- NestJS Mastra routes should only match inside the configured prefix.
- Query identifiers should remain strings and let the route schema decide coercion.

I have a focused fix ready with tests for the workflow barrel registration, route-prefix matching, and query identifier preservation.

title: [FEATURE] Add first-class tool payload projection for display streams and user-visible transcripts
body:
## Summary

Mastra should keep raw tool input/output as the runtime contract, keep `toModelOutput` as the model-facing contract, and add a target-aware tool payload projection boundary used before tool payloads are serialized into AI SDK UI streams, Harness display state, and user-visible transcript/history messages.

Today, tool-heavy production apps need to duplicate sanitizer/projection logic across stream adapters, UI conversion, Harness display state, and transcript persistence.

## Problem

A single tool payload can have different audiences:

- **runtime:** raw input/output for app logic, resume, background tasks, debugging, and internal execution
- **model:** compact model-facing projection via `toModelOutput`
- **display:** browser/UI-safe payload for AI SDK UI streams, React `toUIMessage`, and Harness display state
- **transcript:** user-visible thread/history-safe payload for persisted chat transcript messages

Mastra already has a first-class model-facing projection with `toModelOutput`, but there is no equivalent framework-level projection boundary for display streams or user-visible transcripts.

That means apps need to enforce this boundary manually in every adapter path.

## Current Behavior

Verified against `origin/main` at:

```text
9efa13f3575d681f3231087de80c480b7408d64f
```

Current behavior appears to be:

- `createTool()` supports `toModelOutput`, but there is no equivalent target-aware projection hook for display/transcript payloads.
- `toModelOutput` is model-facing only and should stay that way.
- Tool call/result stream chunks can include raw tool input/output.
- React AI SDK UI conversion can map raw tool input/output into UI tool parts.
- Harness display state/events can carry raw tool args/results.
- User-visible transcript/history persistence needs app-level sanitizers if raw payloads are not appropriate for users.

This is workable for apps that add their own sanitization layer, but the boundary is fragile because every new stream/persistence/display path must remember to apply the same policy.

## Why This Matters

Production tools often return payloads that are useful for runtime code but not appropriate for browser UI state or user-visible transcript history.

Examples include:

- internal IDs
- workspace paths
- source paths
- provider response metadata
- debug scores
- raw API responses
- private document context
- customer-specific fields
- auth-adjacent values
- large payloads that should be summarized for display

Mastra is increasingly used as an application framework around agents: Harness, AI SDK UI integration, HITL, persisted threads, memory, tools, background tasks, and durable workflows. That makes this a framework-level projection boundary, not just an app-level formatting concern.

## Proposed Direction

Add a first-class target-aware tool payload projection policy for payloads leaving runtime.

Possible central API shape:

```ts
toolPayloadPolicy: {
  projectToolPayload({
    target, // 'display' | 'transcript'
    phase,  // 'input-delta' | 'input-available' | 'output-available' | 'error' | 'suspend' | 'resume'
    toolName,
    toolCallId,
    input,
    inputTextDelta,
    output,
    error,
    providerMetadata,
    context,
  }) {
    return projectedPayload;
  },
}
```

The exact names are not important. The key is that projection is:

- target-aware
- phase-aware
- available before browser-facing stream serialization
- available before user-visible transcript/history serialization
- separate from raw runtime payloads
- separate from `toModelOutput`

Optional tool-local defaults could make common cases ergonomic:

```ts
createTool({
  inputSchema,
  outputSchema,

  execute,

  // Existing: model-facing only.
  toModelOutput,

  // Possible ergonomic layer over the central policy.
  payloadProjection: {
    display: {
      input({ input }) {
        return { query: input.query };
      },
      output({ output }) {
        return { summary: output.summary, count: output.items?.length };
      },
      error({ error }) {
        return { message: 'Tool failed' };
      },
    },
    transcript: {
      input({ input }) {
        return { query: input.query };
      },
      output({ output }) {
        return { summary: output.summary, sourceIds: output.sources?.map(s => s.id) };
      },
      error({ error }) {
        return { message: 'Tool failed' };
      },
    },
  },
});
```

## Target Semantics

### Runtime

Raw tool input/output should remain available to runtime code.

This includes app logic, workflow execution, durable resume, background tasks, internal debugging, and any private operational storage that Mastra needs for correctness.

### Model

`toModelOutput` should remain the model-facing projection.

It should not be overloaded to mean "safe for UI" or "safe for transcript."

### Display

Display projection should apply before tool payloads are serialized into:

- AI SDK UI stream parts
- React `toUIMessage` tool parts
- Harness display state/events
- other browser-facing stream adapters

### Transcript

Transcript projection should apply before tool payloads are written into user-visible thread/history messages.

This should not necessarily mean every internal persisted copy is redacted. Mastra may still need private raw storage for durable execution, audit, debugging, or recovery.

## Important Details

### Input must be covered

The projection boundary should cover both tool input and tool output.

Tool input can contain sensitive or noisy values just like tool output.

### Input deltas need special handling

AI SDK UI supports streamed tool input deltas.

If projection is configured and there is no safe delta projector, raw input deltas should be suppressed, masked, or otherwise fail closed rather than streaming raw partial input to the browser.

### Errors should be covered

Tool errors can contain internal stack traces, provider messages, paths, request metadata, or raw payload fragments.

Projection should cover error payloads before display/transcript serialization.

### Suspend/resume and background payloads should be considered

If tool suspension, approval, resume payloads, or background task payloads are displayed or written into user-visible transcript state, they should go through the same projection boundary or be explicitly deferred/documented.

### Provider metadata should be considered

Provider metadata may be safe in some contexts and unsafe/noisy in others. The projection hook should either receive it so apps can decide, or Mastra should define a conservative default.

### Projection failure should fail closed when configured

If a projection policy is configured and projection fails, Mastra should avoid falling back to raw payloads for display/transcript targets.

A reasonable behavior would be:

- emit a generic display/transcript-safe placeholder
- log/trace the projection failure for operators
- preserve raw runtime behavior internally

### Backward compatibility

If no projection policy is configured, current behavior can remain unchanged.

This makes the feature additive and avoids breaking existing apps that expect raw tool payloads in UI parts.

## Related But Distinct

This is related to but distinct from:

- #15943: governance/model hook before tool results feed the next LLM call
- #16039: preserving compact `toModelOutput` history for model context
- #15975: Harness-native AI SDK UI display stream adapter
- #16053: server-history mode for AI SDK UI transport

This issue is specifically about a display/transcript projection boundary for tool payloads leaving runtime.

## Example

A tool call/result might contain:

```ts
{
  toolName: 'lookup_customer',
  toolCallId: 'tc1',
  input: {
    customerId: 'cus_123',
    internalPath: '/workspace/private/customer.json',
  },
  output: {
    displayName: 'Acme',
    apiKey: 'secret-value',
    debugScore: 0.97,
    sourcePath: '/tmp/internal/source.json',
  },
}
```

The raw payload may be useful to runtime code, but a display projection might be:

```ts
{
  input: {
    customerId: 'cus_123',
  },
  output: {
    displayName: 'Acme',
  },
}
```

And a transcript projection might be:

```ts
{
  input: {
    customerId: 'cus_123',
  },
  output: {
    displayName: 'Acme',
  },
}
```

The app should be able to define that once, not separately in every stream adapter, Harness projection, React UI converter, and transcript persistence path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a public projection boundary for tool payloads leaving runtime.
- Projection is target-aware: at minimum `display` and `transcript`.
- Projection is phase-aware: input, input delta, output, error, and future HITL/suspend/resume phases where applicable.
- Raw runtime tool input/output remains unchanged.
- `toModelOutput` remains model-facing only.
- AI SDK UI stream serialization can use display projections.
- React `toUIMessage` conversion can use display projections or already-projected payloads.
- Harness display state/events can use display projections.
- User-visible transcript/history persistence can use transcript projections.
- Tool input as well as tool output is covered.
- Projection failures fail closed for display/transcript targets when a policy is configured.
- No configured projection policy preserves current behavior for backward compatibility.
- Tests cover raw runtime payloads, display-projected payloads, transcript-projected payloads, input deltas, errors, and projection failure behavior.

## Test Plan

Suggested test areas:

- Tool runtime still receives and returns raw payloads.
- `toModelOutput` behavior is unchanged.
- AI SDK UI stream tool-call input uses display projection.
- AI SDK UI stream tool-result output uses display projection.
- Input deltas do not leak raw values when a display policy is configured without a delta projector.
- Harness display state uses display projection.
- User-visible transcript/history writes use transcript projection.
- Raw operational/durable state remains available where Mastra needs it internally.
- Projection errors do not fall back to raw display/transcript payloads.
- No policy configured keeps existing behavior.

## Verification

- [x] I searched open issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I checked this is distinct from `toModelOutput`.
- [x] I checked this is distinct from model-governance hooks and AI SDK transport/history issues.
