If you're experiencing an error, please provide a [minimal reproducible example](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#minimal-reproduction) whenever possible to help us resolve it quickly.

I can reproduce the duplicate-context concern, and while checking it I found a related deeper interaction.

With the documented `SkillSearchProcessor` setup:

```ts
const workspace = new Workspace({
  filesystem: new LocalFilesystem({ basePath: "./project" }),
  skills: ["skills"],
  bm25: true,
})

const skillSearch = new SkillSearchProcessor({ workspace })

const agent = new Agent({
  name: "skill-agent",
  instructions: "Use search_skills to find relevant skills, then load_skill.",
  model,
  workspace,
  inputProcessors: [skillSearch],
})
```

the agent does not only get `search_skills` / `load_skill`.

Because `workspace` is also attached to the agent:

- `Agent.getSkillsProcessors()` still auto-adds the default `SkillsProcessor`, since it only suppresses another processor with `id === "skills-processor"`.
- `Agent.listSkillTools()` still exposes the built-in `skill`, `skill_search`, and `skill_read` tools.
- `Agent.listWorkspaceTools()` still exposes workspace file tools such as `mastra_workspace_read_file`.

So the model can see the same skill through several routes:

- eager available-skill metadata from `SkillsProcessor`
- `search_skills` / `load_skill` from `SkillSearchProcessor`
- `skill` / `skill_search` / `skill_read`
- direct `SKILL.md` reads through workspace file tools

I also tested an alternate setup where the `Workspace` is passed only to `SkillSearchProcessor`, not to the `Agent`. In that case the model only receives `search_skills` / `load_skill`, but then the agent does not receive the normal workspace tools.

My current read is that `SkillSearchProcessor` needs a first-class “on-demand skill mode” contract with `Agent`, rather than each app solving this only with prompt instructions or memory filtering.

A focused framework fix could be:

1. Let `SkillSearchProcessor` advertise that it provides skill discovery/loading.
2. Have `Agent.getSkillsProcessors()` skip auto-adding `SkillsProcessor` when that capability is present.
3. Have `Agent.listSkillTools()` suppress the overlapping `skill` and `skill_search` tools in that mode.
4. Keep `skill_read` available, since it still serves references/scripts/assets and non-filesystem skill sources.
5. Document the remaining workspace-file-tools caveat: `mastra_workspace_read_file` should be reserved for explicit file inspection/editing workflows, not normal skill activation.

I am happy to work on a failing test + PR for this if that direction sounds aligned.

Thanks, this direction aligns with what we are seeing.

One extra data point from our production setup: we already split the workspaces to avoid part of this duplication.

- The Agent receives the normal runtime workspace with built-in workspace skills disabled.
- SkillSearchProcessor receives a processor-only workspace with skills enabled.
- We also mark search_skills/load_skill and legacy skill meta-tools as non-replayable in our app history layer.

That removes the built-in skill/skill_search/skill_read route for normal execution, but the remaining ambiguous route is still the generic workspace file tools reading ./skills/.../SKILL.md or ./default-skills/.../SKILL.md after load_skill has already injected the same instructions.

So I agree this is best solved as a first-class on-demand skill mode contract between SkillSearchProcessor and Agent, plus documentation for the remaining file-tool caveat. A failing test + PR in that direction sounds aligned from our side, and I would be happy to test it against our production setup once available.

title: [BUG] Harness subagent calls are serialized in approval mode
body:
### Describe the Bug

Harness supports configuring multiple subagents with separate instructions, tools, model defaults, and workspace tool allowlists. The built-in `subagent` tool also tells the parent agent to use it when it wants to run multiple investigations in parallel.

In normal harness mode, though, `Harness.sendMessage()` enables global tool approval by passing `requireToolApproval: true` unless `yolo` is enabled. The agent execution workflow treats that global approval flag as a reason to run all tool calls sequentially. As a result, two independent `subagent` tool calls emitted in the same model step run one after the other, even though the harness `subagent` tool itself does not require approval and each spawned subagent runs with its own constrained tools and instructions.

This makes Codex/Claude Code-style delegation slower than expected: a supervisor can ask for parallel read-only exploration subagents, but the harness serializes them in the common safe/default mode.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a `Harness` with at least two `subagents`, for example `explore` and `review`, each with its own `instructions` and read-only/constrained tool set.
2. Leave `initialState.yolo` unset or `false`, so normal approval mode is active.
3. Use a parent agent/model response that emits two `subagent` tool calls in the same step for independent tasks.
4. Observe the emitted `subagent_start`, `subagent_end`, and tool-result timing.
5. The second subagent starts only after the first subagent finishes instead of overlapping.

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

A focused core regression test will be added in this repository. The relevant code paths are:

- `packages/core/src/harness/harness.ts`: `sendMessage()` passes `requireToolApproval: !isYolo`.
- `packages/core/src/harness/tools.ts`: `createSubagentTool()` creates the built-in `subagent` tool and spawns a fresh `Agent` per call.
- `packages/core/src/loop/workflows/agentic-execution/index.ts`: tool-call execution currently serializes when global approval is enabled or when any configured tool requires approval/suspension.
- `packages/core/src/loop/workflows/agentic-execution/tool-call-step.ts`: global approval is applied to each tool call.

### Expected Behavior

Independent harness `subagent` calls should be able to run concurrently in non-yolo mode when the `subagent` tool itself is safe to execute without approval or suspension.

Approval-gated and suspending tools must keep the existing safety behavior:

- ordinary write/edit/execute tools still request approval when configured by harness permissions,
- approval-required or suspending tools still run sequentially,
- safe subagent execution should not bypass approval for tools inside the spawned subagent unless that subagent is explicitly configured with those tools and policies,
- scheduling should be based on the actual tool calls in the current model step, not merely on whether the full configured toolset contains an approval-required tool.

### Environment Information

```block
Repository: mastra-ai/mastra
Package: @mastra/core
Area: Harness, Agents, Tools, agentic execution workflow
Mode affected: normal harness mode with yolo disabled
```

title: filterMessagesForPersistence trims leading/trailing whitespace from individual text parts
body:
## Bug Description

`MessageHistory.filterMessagesForPersistence()` applies `.trim()` to every text part unconditionally, stripping meaningful leading/trailing whitespace from text parts that were split by the new span-based persistence in 1.26.0.

## Location

`src/processors/memory/message-history.ts` — in `filterMessagesForPersistence()`:

```js
if (p.type === `text`) {
    const text = typeof p.text === "string" ? p.text : "";
    return {
        ...p,
        text: removeWorkingMemoryTags(text).trim()  // ← trims every text part
    };
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use `@mastra/core` 1.26.0+ with memory enabled
2. Stream a response from any LLM
3. The new `buildMessagesFromChunks()` stores one text part per text-start/text-end span
4. When the LLM tokenizer splits at word boundaries, some text parts have leading spaces (e.g., `" access"`, `" to"`, `" two"`)
5. `filterMessagesForPersistence` trims each part before saving to storage
6. On recall, the text parts are missing their boundary whitespace

## Observed Behavior

Stream emits text-deltas: `"I have"`, `" access"`, `" to"`, `" two"`, `" skills"`

After persistence and recall, stored parts are: `"I have"`, `"access"`, `"to"`, `"two"`, `"skills"`

When concatenated: `"I haveaccesstotwoskills"` — missing spaces between words.

## Expected Behavior

The `.trim()` should only be applied when `removeWorkingMemoryTags` actually modified the text, or at minimum should not strip single whitespace characters that represent meaningful token boundaries.

Suggested fix:
```js
if (p.type === `text`) {
    const text = typeof p.text === "string" ? p.text : "";
    const cleaned = removeWorkingMemoryTags(text);
    return {
        ...p,
        text: cleaned !== text ? cleaned.trim() : text
    };
}
```

## Environment

- `@mastra/core`: 1.26.0
- `@mastra/memory`: 1.16.0
- `@mastra/libsql`: 1.9.0

## Additional Context

This regression was introduced by PR #15454 ("fix(core): build step messages after stream completes instead of mid-stream") which changed message persistence to store one text part per span. Previously, the mid-stream accumulator produced a single pre-merged text part, so `.trim()` on the whole string had no visible effect. Now that each span becomes its own part, trimming individual parts strips meaningful whitespace at word boundaries.

The `content` string field on the message (from the `.text` getter which joins all parts) also shows `\n` where spaces should be, suggesting the `collapseWhitespace` normalization may also be involved in some code paths.

If you're experiencing an error, please provide a [minimal reproducible example](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#minimal-reproduction) whenever possible to help us resolve it quickly.

FYI: We use our own llm gateway provider and may have had a bug in our provider as well. Both Claude and Cursor are telling me that this bug is still an issue - but the reason why we are seeing it is a bug with our llm gateway sdk: >

Both bugs are real — they just interact. Let me be precise:

The GitHub issue is accurate, but it's describing a Mastra bug that is secondary to a bug in our own code. Here's the distinction:

Our bug (the proximate cause): doStream emitted a unique span ID per token (text-0, text-1, text-2...). This is incorrect usage of the AI SDK v5 span API — the id on text-delta is supposed to identify which span the delta belongs to, not act as a unique delta identifier. Well-behaved providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) emit one text-start / many text-delta (same ID) / one text-end per logical text block. We emitted 33 deltas with 33 different IDs, which Mastra interpreted as 33 separate single-token spans.

Mastra's bug (still real): filterMessagesForPersistence unconditionally .trim()s every text part. Even with correct span usage, a response interleaved with tool calls produces multiple text parts (text before the tool call, text after). The leading/trailing space at those boundaries would be wrongly stripped. The issue accurately describes this and the suggested fix is correct.

So the relationship is:

  | Our bug fixed | Our bug not fixed -- | -- | -- Mastra bug fixed | ✅ Works | ✅ Works Mastra bug not fixed | ✅ Works (our response is 1 part, trim is harmless) | ❌ Broken >

Our fix is sufficient for the whitespace issue today because we now produce a single text part per response, so Mastra's .trim() only touches the outermost edges of the full response string — which is harmless. But the GitHub issue is still worth keeping open: if a response interleaves text and tool calls (two legitimate text spans), Mastra will still trim the boundary whitespace between them incorrectly. That's an independent correctness problem in Mastra that our fix doesn't address.

title: Option to suppress tool call/result rendering in channel adapters
body:
### Problem Statement

When using Mastra's channel adapters (e.g. @chat-adapter/telegram, @chat-adapter/slack) with agents that have tools, the consumeAgentStream method in AgentChannels renders every tool-call and tool-result chunk as a separate message in the chat platform. For agents with multiple tools, this creates a noisy, cluttered experience where the user sees 3-6 intermediate messages with tool names, execution times, and raw result data before the agent's actual response appears. There is currently no way to suppress or customize this behavior.

### Proposed Solution

Proposed Solution

  Add a showToolCalls configuration option to the channels config that controls whether tool call/result chunks are posted as messages:

  channels: {
    adapters: { telegram: createTelegramAdapter() },
    showToolCalls: false,
  }

  When showToolCalls: false, the consumeAgentStream method should skip posting messages for tool-call and tool-result chunk types, only rendering text-delta, step-finish, and finish chunks. The default should remain true for backward compatibility.

### Component

Agents

### Alternatives Considered

  @mastra/core — AgentChannels.consumeAgentStream() (in src/channels/agent-channels.ts)

### Example Use Case

We're building an agent where claims reviewers interact with the AI agent via a Telegram group. The agent has 6 tools (getPendingClaims, checkCoverage, checkAllowance, getClaimDocuments, analyzeReceipt, recordReview). When a reviewer asks "any new claims?", the agent calls 1-4 tools internally before responding. Currently, each tool call renders as a separate Telegram message showing the tool name, execution time, and result data — producing 5+ messages when the reviewer only needs 1 clean summary. We tried overriding channel handlers to use agent.generate() instead of agent.stream(), but generate() doesn't propagate threadId to ObservationalMemory's RequestContext, breaking persistent memory. The default handler is the only path that correctly wires memory, so we can't bypass consumeAgentStream.

### Additional Context

_No response_

**What we implemented:**

**1. Output-only rendering (default for chat adapters)**
Only render the final text response. Tool calls, intermediate results, and execution metadata are suppressed in the user-facing channel.

**2. Configurable verbosity per channel**

While tools execute silently, show a "typing..." indicator so the user knows the agent is working. Without this, suppressing tool calls makes the agent feel unresponsive during long tool chains.

**4. Tool summary on request**
If the user asks "what did you just do?" or "show your work", the agent can reference the suppressed tool calls from the session log.

**The key insight:** chat platforms and API consumers have fundamentally different needs. Chat users want clean output. API consumers want full event streams. The adapter layer should handle this, not the agent.

For agents with 5+ tools (which is common in our 31-agent deployment), the noise reduction from suppressing tool calls improves user satisfaction dramatically. Users stopped asking "why is the bot sending me random stuff?"

@CalebBarnes something to take a look at when you have some time.

The noisy tool-call rendering is a universal UX problem in agent chat interfaces. From building multi-agent chat experiences:

**The solution is a two-layer rendering model**:

1. **Agent layer** — sees everything: tool calls, tool results, intermediate reasoning. This is essential for debugging and for the agent's context window
2. **User layer** — sees only the final response and optionally a collapsed summary of what tools were used. Tool calls render as a single status indicator ("Searching...", "Analyzing data..."), not as separate messages

**Implementation pattern**: The channel adapter should buffer tool-call and tool-result chunks, aggregate them into a single status update (collapsible in the UI), and only render the final assistant response as a full message. This is essentially progressive context compaction for the user-facing stream — the agent sees full detail, the user sees a summary.

**The memory implication**: When storing conversation history, store the full trace (including tool calls) but mark tool messages as "system-internal." Memory retrieval for context window construction can then choose: full trace for debugging/replay, user-visible messages only for context efficiency. We found this reduces context window usage by ~40% without losing behavioral quality.

**Rate limiting tool status updates**: For agents that make 5+ tool calls in sequence, even status updates become noisy. Batch updates: "Used 3 tools: web search, calculator, code execution" as a single message, not three separate ones.

title: [FEATURE] Add prompt-only model context for initial input processors
body:
## Problem Statement

Initial input processors can currently shape the first model prompt only by returning `messages`, which mutates or replaces the canonical conversation state. That couples two different concerns: the durable message list used by memory, persistence, tool state, and later turns, and the model input for one prompt.

Agentic loop input-step processors already have a prompt-only channel through `modelContextMessages`. The initial `processInput` path does not have the same capability, so processors that need to preload, filter, or limit context before the first model call have to either mutate canonical messages or build custom wrappers around native processors.

## Proposed Solution

Allow initial `processInput` processors to return `modelContextMessages` with the same prompt-only semantics used by `processInputStep`:

- `messages` mutates or replaces canonical messages.
- `modelContextMessages` changes the next model prompt only.
- A single processor result cannot return both `messages` and `modelContextMessages`.
- Once prompt-only mode begins, later processors receive the prompt-only list as their input messages while the canonical `MessageList` remains intact.
- Prompt-only messages should not be persisted to memory or written into canonical message rows.
- System prompt changes should continue to use `systemMessages`; system-role entries in prompt-only messages should not override canonical system messages.

This keeps the existing public agent execution model and extends the already-established step processor contract to the initial input path.

## Alternatives Considered

Using `systemMessages` is not equivalent because transcript-shaped context is not the same as changing the system prompt, and system precedence rules are different.

Returning canonical `messages` works for prompt shaping but can damage memory, persistence, replay, selected-version continuation, and future turns because synthetic or filtered prompt context becomes indistinguishable from durable conversation state.

Passing extra data through request context leaves native processors, token limiters, tool-call filters, observability, and retry paths without a consistent message channel to inspect.

Adding a brand-new processor context abstraction could solve this more broadly, but it is larger than necessary for this gap. `modelContextMessages` already exists on step processors, so parity on initial processors is the smallest consistent API.

## Example Use Case

A processor may need to inject retrieved transcript context, compacted prior conversation text, or one-call-only safety context before the first model call. That context should participate in filtering and token limiting for the immediate prompt, but it should not become durable memory or appear as canonical conversation history in future turns.

## Additional Context

This would make initial input processors and agentic loop step processors follow the same prompt-only chaining model, which reduces custom wrapper logic around native processors and makes observability clearer by separating canonical message count from model input count.

## Verification

title: [BUG] Internal server errors and stack traces are leaked to client-side responses
body:
### Describe the Bug

Internal server errors, including full stack traces and environment paths, are being returned directly to the client-side UI. This occurs not only with custom Tools but also with general Agent/API errors (e.g., AI SDK provider errors). This poses a security risk and results in a poor user experience.

claude say:
1. Analysis of Current Implementation
I’ve investigated the codebase and identified the potential cause of this information leak. The issue resides in how the streaming response is constructed using the AI SDK's toDataStreamResponse.

Specifically, in the generated chunk (e.g., chunk-FCNSMQDH.js or equivalent in @mastra/core), the getErrorMessage handler passes the raw error message or the entire error object to the client:

```JavaScript
const streamResponse = streamResult.toDataStreamResponse({
  getErrorMessage: (error) => {
    // This exposes error.message or the full stringified object to the frontend
    return `An error occurred while processing your request. ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : JSON.stringify(error)}`;
  }
});
```
2. Impact
Case 1 (Error instance): error.message often contains provider-specific details (e.g., Anthropic/Google Vertex error details), which can include internal configuration hints or resource names.

Case 2 (Plain Object): If the error is not an instance of Error, JSON.stringify(error) is returned, which potentially leaks the entire state of the error object, including metadata and internal paths.

While the non-streaming (REST) path seems to be handled via HTTPException (returning only this.message), the streaming path is currently unsanitized.

3. Comparison with Existing Issues
I searched through GitHub Issues but couldn't find an exact match for this leak in the streaming protocol:

#5309 addressed the opposite problem (errors being swallowed).

#12644 was related to server-side logging of API keys.
There is currently no open issue regarding the sanitization of toDataStreamResponse in Mastra.

4. Proposed Fix
We should implement a way to sanitize or override getErrorMessage globally within the Mastra configuration, or at least ensure that sensitive fields (stack, internal paths, config) are stripped by default in production mode.

### Steps To Reproduce

When an underlying error occurs (such as an empty message block or an authentication failure), the raw error object is serialized and sent to the frontend.

Example Error Output (Masked):
```
{
  "message": "messages: text content blocks must be non-empty",
  "name": "AI_APICallError",
  "stack": "AI_APICallError: messages: text content blocks must be non-empty\\n at [MASKED_PATH]/node_modules/.pnpm/@ai-sdk+provider-utils@.../dist/index.mjs:2349:14\\n at async AnthropicMessagesLanguageModel.doStream (...)\\n at async AISDKV6LanguageModel.doStream (...)",
  "cause": { ... }
}
```

Current Behavior

Mastra seems to pass the entire error object from the server/agent execution directly to the client response, exposing internal file structures and dependency versions.

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

Source code analysis provided

### Expected Behavior

- In production mode, internal error details (especially stack) should be stripped.
- The framework should provide a way to intercept or sanitize these errors before they reach the client.
- Users should be able to return a user-friendly error message instead of the raw technical error.

### Environment Information

```block
nodejs, ts
```

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

title: Feature Request - Production sandbox design
body:
This issue was created from Discord post 1498329615758917793:

[![Open in Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open_in_Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/channels/1309558646228779139/1498329615758917793)

Similar to how other coding harnesses work (Claude Code, Cursor), it would be cool to be able to have two execute_command tools (or Mastra should make it so you can set this up):

- One execute_command tool that executes without approvals, but with a sandbox wrapper
- One execute_command tool that executes outside the sandbox, but requires user approval

Right now, you can only pass in one sandbox implementation and it is always attached to execute_command

comments.body:
Thank you for reporting this issue! We have labeled it for trio-tb and we will look into it as soon as possible.

If you're experiencing an error, please provide a [minimal reproducible example](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#minimal-reproduction) whenever possible to help us resolve it quickly.

The two-tool pattern you're describing, sandboxed-but-automatic vs unsandboxed-but-gated, is a reasonable model, but the distinction worth making explicit is that the sandbox and the approval gate are orthogonal controls. A sandboxed tool probably should still have an approval option for cases where the sandbox isn't trusted to contain the blast radius. An unsandboxed tool gated by approval still depends on the human approver knowing what they're approving.

A cleaner abstraction might be a risk tier on each tool: tier 0 runs freely inside the sandbox, tier 1 runs inside the sandbox but with approval, tier 2 runs outside the sandbox with mandatory approval. That gives you more than two modes without requiring multiple tool registrations.

For the implementation, the key is that the approval gate needs to be synchronous with tool execution, the agent can't proceed until the approval resolves, which means your harness needs an async approval channel that can block the tool call without blocking the whole event loop.

title: Workflow suspend/resume breaks when the workflow is owned by a specialist agent
body:
This issue was created from Discord post 1497260872173748325:

[![Open in Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open_in_Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/channels/1309558646228779139/1497260872173748325)

Anyone run into workflow suspend/resume breaking when the workflow lives on a specialist agent?

Setup is pretty vanilla: supervisor with an `agents` resolver exposing a specialist, specialist owns a workflow that suspends for human in the loop. Call resumeStream on the supervisor with the runId from the suspend when the user responds. The supervisor's loop resumes, the specialist's loop resumes, but the inner workflow just restarts from step 1 instead of picking up where it left off.

Dug around and it looks like the sub-agent gets a brand new thread id every time the supervisor re-enters the delegation — including on resume. So the suspended tool metadata that was saved in the original sub-agent thread is unreachable the second time around, and the workflow ends up with a fresh runId.

Is there a workaround for this other than putting the workflow directly on the supervisor? Kind of defeats the whole point of splitting into specialists if every suspendable workflow has to live at the top level.

The suspend/resume breaking on specialist agents is a known class of architectural issues in multi-agent workflow systems.

From building persistent workflow resumption for multi-agent teams:

**Root cause pattern**: When a workflow is owned by a specialist agent (not the supervisor), the suspend serializes context relative to the specialist — but the resume path goes through the supervisor, which reconstructs context differently. The agent identity mismatch between suspend and resume causes the state deserialization to fail or produce unexpected behavior.

**The fix pattern — agent-independent state serialization**: The suspended workflow state should be serialized with agent-independent identifiers:
1. **Task state** — current step, completed steps with outputs, pending decisions (structured, not agent-specific conversation format)
2. **Workflow context** — the full workflow graph, current position, branching history
3. **Agent assignment** — which agent was executing when suspended (so resume can route to the same agent)

This is essentially a STATE.json pattern: a machine-readable snapshot that any agent in the system can use to reconstruct the workflow state.

**Progressive context compaction for resume**: Don't replay the full conversation history on resume. Compact to: current step description + previous step results (structured summary with entity references preserved verbatim) + workflow-level constraints. This is cheaper in tokens and more reliable than conversation replay.

**Checkpoint-based resumability**: For long workflows, checkpoint at every step completion (not just on suspend). This way, if a resume fails, you can roll back to the last successful checkpoint rather than starting from scratch. Each checkpoint includes: (step_id, outputs, agent_state_hash, timestamp).

Architecture on persistent state management: https://blog.kinthai.ai/why-character-ai-forgets-you-persistent-memory-architecture
Multi-agent coordination: https://blog.kinthai.ai/221-agents-multi-agent-coordination-lessons

title: Typechecked Workflow Outputs
body:
This issue was created from Discord post 1497258249731178707:

[![Open in Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open_in_Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/channels/1309558646228779139/1497258249731178707)

Is it normal that workflow outputs aren't typechecked properly?

Given a workflow like this:
```ts
export const createPrWorkflow = createWorkflow({
  id: "Create PR",
  description:
    "Repo-agnostic PR creation: list changes, draft, list PRs, supervisor duplicate check, upsert + open or skip.",
  inputSchema: createPrWorkflowInputSchema,
  outputSchema: createPrWorkflowOutputSchema,
})
  .then(createEmptyInput)
  .then(getChangedPathsForPrDraft)
  .then(createDraftPrompt)
  .then(draftPr)
  .then(getInFlightPrs)
  .then(createSupervisorPrompt)
  .then(checkDuplicatePr)
  .then(createBranchDecision)
  .branch([
    [
      ({ inputData }) => Promise.resolve(inputData.isDuplicate === false),
      openPrWorkflow,
    ],
    [
      ({ inputData }) => Promise.resolve(inputData.isDuplicate !== false),
      skipDuplicatePr,
    ],
  ])
  .map(({ inputData }) => {
    return Promise.resolve(123);
  })
  .commit();
```

- This workflow defines an outputSchema with a complex object.
- As my last step of the workflow, I map to `123`, which doesn't satisfy the outputSchema.

Expectation: typechecker should inform me that my map is wrong
Reality: Typecheck passes

This type of behavior makes it really hard to make reliable workflows, because I end up discovering bugs at runtime instead of at compile time.

title: [FEATURE] Add Channels Support to the Harness Class
body:
### Problem Statement

Channels (added in `@mastra/core@1.22.0`) let agents respond to messages on Slack, Discord, and Telegram — but they can only be configured on individual `Agent` instances. This makes channels fundamentally incompatible with `Harness`.
 
When a message arrives on a channel connected to an individual agent, that agent handles it in complete isolation. The harness is never involved. There is no mode-switching, no shared thread state, no harness tool approvals, no `harness.subscribe()` events, no observational memory, no subagent routing — none of the orchestration that is the entire point of using a harness. A user messaging that Slack bot is not talking to the harness. They are talking directly to one agent, as if the harness did not exist.
 
Concretely, there is no `channels` option on `new Harness()`. There is no way to start or stop channel listeners through the harness lifecycle. There are no channel-related events emitted through `harness.subscribe()`. And there is no webhook path tied to a harness ID — only to individual agent IDs.
 
Real-world use cases this blocks entirely:
 
- A Slack-connected coding harness that routes planning conversations to a plan agent and implementation work to a build agent — impossible without harness-level channel routing
- A Discord support harness with triage, escalation, and resolution modes — each incoming message must enter the harness pipeline, not land on a single isolated agent
- A Telegram harness running `gather → analyse → publish` modes — needs one bot, one entry point, and the full harness orchestrating which agent responds
- A customer-onboarding harness with a per-customer Slack channel and per-customer thread — thread lifecycle must be managed by the harness, not by individual agents acting independently
- Any harness where tool approval cards, mode-switching, or observational memory need to work over a messaging platform


### Proposed Solution


Add a top-level `channels` option to the `Harness` constructor. The config applies to all modes. Per-mode agent-level `channels` settings take precedence where set, so the harness option covers the common case and individual overrides remain possible.
 
The harness lifecycle (`init()` / `destroy()`) starts and stops channel listeners automatically. Incoming channel messages are routed through `sendMessage()` so all existing harness features — tool approvals, mode-switching, observational memory, permissions — work transparently.
 
All modes and adapters share a common config shape modelled on the existing agent-level `channels` option:
 
```ts
interface HarnessChannelsConfig {
  adapters: Record<string, ChatAdapter>
  threadContext?: { maxMessages?: number }
  inlineMedia?: string[]
  inlineLinks?: (string | { match: string; mimeType: string })[]
}
```
 
`threadContext.maxMessages` controls how many prior platform messages are fetched on first mention before Mastra memory takes over. `inlineMedia` and `inlineLinks` allow multimodal content to be forwarded to the model, identical to the existing agent-level behaviour.
 
Incoming channel messages route to the currently active mode. Calling `switchMode()` redirects subsequent channel messages to the new mode's agent without touching the adapter config.
 
Four new methods are added to the harness:
 
- `startChannels()` — starts all configured adapters; called automatically by `init()`
- `stopChannels()` — stops all active listeners; called automatically by `destroy()`
- `getChannelWebhookPath({ platform })` — returns the webhook path for programmatic platform registration
- `listActiveChannels()` — returns platform names with active listeners
Five new events are emitted through `harness.subscribe()`:
 
| Event | Description |
|---|---|
| `channel_message_received` | A message arrived from a platform. Includes `platform`, `threadId`, `userId`, `content`. |
| `channel_message_sent` | The harness sent a response back to a platform thread. |
| `channel_started` | An adapter started successfully. Includes `platform`. |
| `channel_stopped` | An adapter stopped. Includes `platform`. |
| `channel_error` | An adapter encountered an error. Includes `platform`, `error`. |
 
Webhook routes follow the existing agent-level pattern, scoped to the harness ID:
 
```
/api/agents/{harnessId}/channels/{platform}/webhook
```
 

### Component

Other, Agents, Tools, Integrations,Agents, Harness, Server, Channels

### Alternatives Considered

**Configure channels per-agent** — this is the root of the problem, not an alternative. When a channel message arrives on an agent configured with `channels`, that agent handles it directly and independently. The harness is never invoked, `harness.sendMessage()` is never called, and the entire orchestration layer — mode-switching, tool approvals, observational memory, shared thread state — is bypassed. A user messaging that bot is not talking to the harness. For any use case that requires harness orchestration over a messaging platform, per-agent channel config simply does not work.
 
**Use Chat SDK's `Chat` class directly alongside the harness** — Chat SDK ships its own [`Chat` class](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/adapters#using-multiple-adapters) with multi-adapter support and its own state layer (Redis, etc.). Wiring it up independently means two event systems, two state stores, and a manual bridge to get messages into `harness.sendMessage()` — re-implementing streaming, tool approvals, and multi-user prefixing that the harness already handles. The result is more code and less capability than a native integration.
 
**Add `channels` to `HarnessMode` instead of the top-level constructor** — would allow per-mode adapter config, but the common case is the same adapters across all modes. A top-level option covers that cleanly; per-agent config already handles the per-mode override without adding a new `HarnessMode` field.

### Example Use Case

A developer building a team coding assistant wants a single Slack bot that routes planning conversations to a planning agent and implementation work to a build agent — all under one harness, one Slack app, one webhook URL — with no adapter config duplicated across agent files.
 
```ts
import { Harness } from '@mastra/core/harness'
import { LibSQLStore } from '@mastra/libsql'
import { createSlackAdapter } from '@chat-adapter/slack'
import { z } from 'zod'
 
// Single harness — channels declared once, apply to all modes
const harness = new Harness({
  id: 'team-coding-assistant',
  storage: new LibSQLStore({ url: process.env.DATABASE_URL }),
  stateSchema: z.object({
    currentModelId: z.string().optional(),
  }),
 
  channels: {
    adapters: {
      slack: createSlackAdapter(),   // reads SLACK_BOT_TOKEN from env
    },
    threadContext: { maxMessages: 10 },
    inlineMedia: ['image/*'],
  },
 
  modes: [
    { id: 'plan',   name: 'Plan',   default: true, agent: planAgent   },
    { id: 'build',  name: 'Build',                 agent: buildAgent  },
    { id: 'review', name: 'Review',                agent: reviewAgent },
  ],
})
 
// Subscribe to channel events alongside existing harness events
harness.subscribe(event => {
  switch (event.type) {
    case 'channel_message_received':
      console.log(`[${event.platform}] ${event.userId}: ${event.content}`)
      break
    case 'channel_error':
      alertOps(event.platform, event.error)
      break
    case 'message_update':
      renderToTUI(event.message)
      break
  }
})
 
// init() starts the Slack listener automatically
await harness.init()
await harness.selectOrCreateThread()
 
// Webhook path to register in the Slack app dashboard
console.log(harness.getChannelWebhookPath({ platform: 'slack' }))
// '/api/agents/team-coding-assistant/channels/slack/webhook'
 
// Mid-session: switch to build mode — subsequent Slack messages
// are now handled by buildAgent, no adapter change needed
await harness.switchMode({ modeId: 'build' })
 
// Inspect active adapters
console.log(harness.listActiveChannels()) // ['slack']
 
// Cleanup — stopChannels() called automatically
await harness.destroy()
```

### Additional Context
 
**More use cases this unlocks:**
 
| Use Case | Mode pattern | Channel pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Team coding assistant | `plan → build → review` | Single Slack bot, mode switch on user command |
| Customer support harness | `triage → escalate → resolve` | Discord server, one webhook, shared adapter |
| Content pipeline bot | `research → draft → publish` | Telegram bot per workspace |
| Security ops harness | `detect → investigate → remediate` | Slack + PagerDuty, multimodal screenshots inline |
| Patient care harness | `review → draft → notify` | Per-patient Slack channel, per-patient thread |
| Competitive intel harness | `scrape → analyse → brief` | Slack briefing channel, stateful thread |
 
**Peer comparison:**
- Channels already exist on `Agent` — this is a lift-and-shift to `Harness`, not a new concept
- [Chat SDK adapters](https://chat-sdk.dev/adapters) — Slack, Discord, Telegram adapters available today
**References:**
- [Channels docs](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/channels)
- [Harness class reference](https://mastra.ai/reference/harness/harness-class)
- [Tool approval docs](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/agent-approval)
- [Chat SDK adapters](https://chat-sdk.dev/adapters)


### Verification

- [x] I have provided sufficient context for the team to understand the request

title: [BUG] file_search tool-results dropped when combined with any other tool → "Corrupted tool call context" on next turn (Gemini 3)
body:
## Describe the Bug

Gemini 3 officially supports combining `file_search` with function-calling tools ([docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/tool-combination)). Through Mastra, the first turn works, but when any second tool is registered alongside `google.tools.fileSearch`, tool-results from `file_search` are dropped by `MessageMerger.updateToolInvocation` and the next turn fails:

```
AI_APICallError: contents[N].parts[0]: Corrupted tool call context.
status: 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT
```

On the turn `file_search` runs, Mastra logs one or more:

```
updateToolInvocation: no matching tool call found for toolCallId=<id>
```

Each warning is a dropped `file_search` result — the corresponding tool-call was already in `this.messages` but the arriving result's `toolCallId` did not match, so the result was never appended. The persisted assistant message ends up with a tool-call whose state never advances to `result`; on the next turn the replay to Gemini is therefore incomplete.

### Notes

- `@mastra/core@1.27.0` already sets `includeServerSideToolInvocations: true` and forwards `thoughtSignature`, so the combined-tools request itself is configured correctly — which matches the first turn succeeding.
- Removing the second tool (leaving `file_search` alone) → no warning, both turns succeed.
- Reproduces on both `@mastra/libsql@1.9.0` and `@mastra/pg@1.9.2` → not storage-specific, so not a re-occurrence of #15183.
- Different from the Google-side regression in [this forum thread](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/gemini-3-flash-preview-tool-use-with-function-calling-is-unsupported-when-combining-filesearch-with-functiondeclarations-worked-last-week/123341) — that bug rejects the *first* turn; here the first turn works and the *second* fails.

## Steps To Reproduce

**`package.json`**

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": { "repro": "tsx --env-file=.env src/repro.ts" },
  "dependencies": {
    "@ai-sdk/google": "3.0.64",
    "@mastra/core": "1.27.0",
    "@mastra/libsql": "1.9.0",
    "@mastra/memory": "1.17.0",
    "zod": "4.3.6"
  },
  "devDependencies": { "tsx": "4.20.3", "typescript": "5.9.2" }
}
```

**`src/repro.ts`**

```ts
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google'
import { Mastra } from '@mastra/core'
import { Agent } from '@mastra/core/agent'
import { createTool } from '@mastra/core/tools'
import { LibSQLStore } from '@mastra/libsql'
import { Memory } from '@mastra/memory'
import { z } from 'zod'

const GEMINI_API_KEY = process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY!
const FILE_SEARCH_STORE = process.env.FILE_SEARCH_STORE! // e.g. "fileSearchStores/my-store"

// Any second tool triggers the bug — body is never called. Remove it → bug disappears.
const echoTool = createTool({
  id: 'echo',
  description: 'Echoes text. Do not call unless asked.',
  inputSchema: z.object({ text: z.string() }),
  execute: async ({ text }) => ({ echoed: text }),
})

const agent = new Agent({
  id: 'chat',
  name: 'Chat',
  instructions: 'You are a helpful assistant. Use file_search for questions about the user\'s documents.',
  model: { id: 'google/gemini-3-flash-preview', apiKey: GEMINI_API_KEY },
  tools: {
    file_search: google.tools.fileSearch({ fileSearchStoreNames: [FILE_SEARCH_STORE] }),
    echo: echoTool,
  },
  memory: new Memory({
    options: {
      observationalMemory: { model: { id: 'google/gemini-2.5-flash', apiKey: GEMINI_API_KEY } },
    },
  }),
})

const mastra = new Mastra({
  agents: { chat: agent },
  storage: new LibSQLStore({ id: 'repro', url: 'file:./repro.db' }),
})

async function turn(input: string, thread: string) {
  console.log(`\n=== USER: ${input} ===`)
  const s = await mastra.getAgent('chat').stream(input, { memory: { thread, resource: 'u1' } })
  for await (const c of s.textStream) process.stdout.write(c)
  process.stdout.write('\n')
  if (s.error) throw s.error
}

const thread = `repro-${Date.now()}`
await turn('What documents do I have?', thread)
await turn('Tell me more about one of them.', thread)
```

### Run

1. `pnpm install`
2. Create `.env` with `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `FILE_SEARCH_STORE=fileSearchStores/<your-store>` (store must contain at least one indexed document).
3. `pnpm repro`

### Observed output (both tools registered)

```
=== USER: What documents do I have? ===
```

comments.body:
Thank you for reporting this issue! We have labeled it for trio-tb and we will look into it as soon as possible.

If you're experiencing an error, please provide a [minimal reproducible example](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#minimal-reproduction) whenever possible to help us resolve it quickly.

Fix submitted in #15709.

**Root cause:** `MessageList.updateToolInvocation()` only matched by exact `toolCallId`. When Google's server-side tools (like `file_search`) are combined with function-calling tools, the `@ai-sdk/google` provider may assign different IDs to the `tool-call` and `tool-result` chunks, causing all results to be silently dropped.

**Fix:** Added a fallback that matches provider-executed tool results by `toolName` when the exact `toolCallId` lookup fails. The fallback only activates for tools with `providerExecuted: true` and `state: 'call'`, so client-executed tools (which always have stable IDs) are unaffected.

body:
This issue was created from Discord post 1496834097652170864:

# Feature Request: Per-Agent Execution Timeout with Fallback Trigger

## Discord Draft (Short)

Hi Mastra team,

we need a way to control **maximum runtime per agent run** (not only per tool/background task), so an agent cannot get stuck and we can trigger a fallback strategy automatically.

### Problem

Today we can configure:

- global server/request timeout
- background task timeout (tool/task-level)
- wait timeout for background task synchronization

What is missing is a **hard timeout for total agent runtime** (full loop budget).

### Requested Feature

- Agent-level runtime budget, e.g. `maxExecutionMs`
- Timeout behavior policy, e.g.:
  - `fallback-model`
  - `return-partial`
  - `fail`
  - optional `continue-in-background`

### Why this matters

- Prevent stuck runs
- Keep predictable latency/SLAs
- Trigger reliable model fallback when runtime budget is exceeded

---

## GitHub Draft (Detailed)

### Title

Add per-agent execution timeout with timeout-based fallback policy

### Summary

Please add a configurable **agent-level execution timeout** that limits the total runtime of one agent run across reasoning loops, tool orchestration, and retries.

When timeout is reached, apply a deterministic strategy (especially model fallback).

### Current Gap

Current controls mainly cover:

- server-level HTTP timeout
- background task timeout (tool/task-level)
- waiting behavior for background tasks

But there is no first-class setting for:

> "How long may this specific agent run in total before timeout policy must apply?"

title: [FEATURE] Support dynamic sandbox resolution via requestContext in Workspace

comments.body:
Hey @finreinhard Thanks for this feature request , I will take a look on it :)
Same pattern as #13150 (dynamic filesystem), just for sandbox we need to do .

Dynamic sandbox resolution per request is essential for multi-tenant deployments.

We run 31 agents serving multiple user groups at KinthAI, and static sandbox configuration means all users share the same workspace isolation — which is not isolation at all.

**What requestContext-based sandbox resolution enables:**

1. **Per-user workspace isolation**
```ts
sandbox: (context) => new LocalSandbox({
  workingDirectory: path.join("./workspaces", context.userId),
  permissions: getUserPermissions(context.userId)
})
```
Each user gets their own filesystem sandbox. User A cannot access User B files.

2. **Per-agent sandbox profiles**
Different agents need different sandbox capabilities:
- Coding agent: full filesystem, network access
- Content agent: read-only filesystem, no network
- Admin agent: elevated permissions

3. **Dynamic resource limits**
```ts
sandbox: (context) => new LocalSandbox({
  memoryLimit: context.user.tier === "premium" ? "4gb" : "1gb",
  timeout: context.user.tier === "premium" ? 300000 : 60000
})
```

The current static sandbox forces you to either over-provision (expensive) or under-provision (limits capability) for all users equally.

This aligns with the broader pattern we see across agent platforms: anything that touches isolation (sandbox, memory, sessions, media) needs per-request scoping in multi-tenant deployments.

Related architecture: [OpenClaw Multi-Tenancy: Why VM-Per-User Does Not Scale](https://blog.kinthai.ai/openclaw-multi-tenancy-why-vm-per-user-doesnt-scale)

[@mastra/clickhouse] Support Replicated* table engines for multi-replica ClickHouse clusters
body:
### Problem Statement

`@mastra/clickhouse` (both the classic `ObservabilityStorageClickhouse` and the v-next `ObservabilityStorageClickhouseVNext`) emits DDL using plain `MergeTree` / `ReplacingMergeTree` engines. On a multi-replica (non-sharded) ClickHouse cluster — a very common production topology where writes and reads are load-balanced across replicas behind an HTTP endpoint — plain engines do **not** replicate data across nodes. Each replica ends up with its own disjoint slice of writes.

The user-visible symptom in Mastra Studio is severe "split-brain" behaviour:

- Trace/span counts on the observability pages change on every refresh (e.g. 3 traces, then 2, then 1, then 3 again) as the HTTP load balancer rotates across replicas.
- Individual trace pages show "no spans for this trace" intermittently — the trace row was written to replica A, the spans to replica B.
- Scores, logs and metrics appear and disappear the same way.

We confirmed this by querying each replica directly: `mastra_trace_events` on replica 0-0-0 had all 3 traces, replica 0-1-0 had only 1. Same story for `mastra_span_events`, `mastra_score_events`, etc. The newly-added `mastra_discovery_pairs` table in v-next has the same problem — our cluster operator flagged that it is created as `ENGINE = MergeTree` when it should be `ReplicatedMergeTree` for our topology.

Pinning all ClickHouse traffic to a single replica via a Node `http.Agent` with `maxSockets: 1` + keep-alive reduces the frequency of the divergence (it forces a single TCP socket), but it is not a real fix: any connection reset (idle timeout at the load balancer, pod restart, network hiccup) re-rolls the replica and the split-brain returns. It also obviously does not scale — it defeats the point of having replicas.

The only real fix today is for the operator to manually `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree(...)` for every Mastra observability table before Mastra initialises, which (a) requires knowing the full, evolving Mastra schema ahead of time, (b) breaks every time Mastra adds a new table (as happened with `mastra_discovery_pairs` in v-next), and (c) is not documented anywhere.

### Proposed Solution

Let `@mastra/clickhouse` emit `Replicated*` engines when the target ClickHouse cluster is multi-replica. Any of these would solve it; listed in rough order of preference:

1. **Config option on the storage class.** E.g.

   ```ts
   new ObservabilityStorageClickhouseVNext({
     client,
     engine: "replicated", // or: { cluster: "{cluster}", zooPath: "..." }
   });
   ```

   Internally this swaps `MergeTree` → `ReplicatedMergeTree(zooPath, replica)` and `ReplacingMergeTree(ver)` → `ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree(zooPath, replica, ver)` for every table it owns, and optionally appends `ON CLUSTER '{cluster}'` to DDL. Using the `{shard}` / `{replica}` macros keeps the zoo path generic.

2. **Honor server-side `default_table_engine`.** ClickHouse lets you set `default_table_engine = 'ReplicatedMergeTree'` at the cluster level, which auto-rewrites `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = MergeTree` on the fly. Mastra currently passes explicit engine strings which bypass this. If the storage class had an option to emit "unspecified" engines (or used `CREATE TABLE ... AS ...` without `ENGINE =`), operators could handle replication entirely server-side with no library changes.

3. **Auto-detect.** Query `system.clusters` / `system.replicas` on init and pick `Replicated*` automatically when the connected instance is part of a replicated cluster. More magic, but would "just work".

Whichever path is chosen, please apply it uniformly — including to any tables added in future versions (the recent `mastra_discovery_pairs` addition is what re-broke us). A single internal helper that wraps every `CREATE TABLE` would keep this consistent going forward.

Docs should also call out explicitly that the current defaults are **not safe** on multi-replica clusters — right now this is a silent footgun.

### Component

Memory

### Alternatives Considered

Two workarounds we've tried, neither of which is a real fix:

1. **Pin client traffic to a single replica.** Pass a custom `http.Agent` with `keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 1, keepAliveMsecs: 60_000` to `@clickhouse/client`'s `createClient` via `http_agent`. This serialises all Mastra's ClickHouse traffic onto one TCP socket, so as long as the socket stays alive it lands on one replica and reads/writes are consistent. Any socket reset (ingress idle timeout, pod restart) re-rolls the replica and the split-brain returns. It also obviously kills the point of having replicas.

2. **Pre-create the tables with `Replicated*` engines before Mastra starts.** Works, but is brittle: requires mirroring Mastra's internal schema (column types, ordering keys, TTLs) and breaks on every Mastra release that adds or changes a table — which is how we hit `mastra_discovery_pairs` in v-next.

Neither workaround addresses the new tables Mastra adds in future versions, which is the core of the feature request: we need the library itself to emit replication-safe DDL (or at least provide a supported hook for operators to control engine choice).

### Example Use Case

As a platform engineer running Mastra against a production multi-replica ClickHouse cluster, I want `@mastra/clickhouse` to emit replication-safe DDL (either automatically or via an explicit config option) so that traces, spans, scores, logs and metrics are consistent across all replicas and Mastra Studio shows stable, correct data regardless of which replica the HTTP load balancer picks for a given request.

### Additional Context

**Environment / versions affected**

- `@mastra/clickhouse` 1.5.0 (`ObservabilityStorageClickhouseVNext`) — confirmed reproducer
- `@mastra/core` 1.26.0, `@mastra/observability` 1.10.0
- `@clickhouse/client` 1.18.2
- ClickHouse 24.x, Altinity Operator, 2 replicas, no sharding, HTTP load balancer in front
- Node 22 / TypeScript

**Tables we observed the split-brain on**

- `mastra_trace_events`
- `mastra_span_events`
- `mastra_log_events`
- `mastra_metric_events`
- `mastra_score_events`
- `mastra_feedback_events`
- `mastra_discovery_pairs` (new in v-next; called out explicitly by our cluster operator as being created with `ENGINE = MergeTree` when it should be `ReplicatedMergeTree`)

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have provided sufficient context for the team to understand the request

title: [BUG] @mastra/client-js only picks one tool-invocation from a tool-calls step before continuing
body:
### Describe the Bug

I think there is a bug in the client-side continuation logic in @mastra/client-js for streamed client tools.

  ### Core issue

  In the processStreamResponse(...) continuation path, when a step finishes with finishReason === 'tool-calls', the client appears to collect only one tool invocation from the assistant
  message:

```typescript
  const toolCall = [...(message?.parts ?? [])]
    .reverse()
    .find(part => part.type === 'tool-invocation')?.toolInvocation;
  if (toolCall) {
    toolCalls.push(toolCall);
  }
```

  Because this uses reverse().find(...), it selects only the last tool-invocation part from the message.

  So even though the code later loops over toolCalls, it is not actually collecting all tool invocations from the finished step.

  ### Why this matters

  If a streamed assistant step contains multiple client tool invocations, the client should:

  1. collect all pending tool-invocation parts from that step
  2. execute each pending client tool once
  3. patch all of their results into the assistant message
  4. recurse once with the fully updated message set

  The current code does not appear to do that.

  ### Secondary problem

  Executed tool calls are not removed from the toolCalls array before later continuations. That means the current structure can also reprocess previously seen tool calls.

  So the current behavior seems to be:

  1. collect one tool invocation from the finished step
  2. append it to an accumulated toolCalls array
  3. loop over that accumulated array
  4. recurse once per tool call

  That is different from “handle all tool calls from the current step.”

  ### Why I’m filing this

  We tested this in a real frontend using native MastraClient.getAgent(...).stream(...) and a single client meta-tool. That still failed whenever the run required repeated client-tool
  continuation.

  Server-only prompts succeeded.
  Client-tool runs that required repeated client continuations did not.

  This lines up with the code above: using a single meta-tool name does not help if the assistant can emit that same client tool multiple times in the same step, because only one
  invocation is harvested from the message.

  ### Suggested fix direction

  Instead of:

```typescript
  const toolCall = [...(message?.parts ?? [])]
    .reverse()
    .find(part => part.type === 'tool-invocation')?.toolInvocation;
```

  the client should gather all pending tool invocations from the message, something conceptually like:

```typescript
  const pendingToolCalls = (message?.parts ?? [])
    .filter(part => part.type === 'tool-invocation')
    .map(part => part.toolInvocation)
    .filter(toolInvocation => toolInvocation?.state === 'call');
```

  Then:

  1. execute each matching client tool once
  2. patch all results into a cloned lastMessage
  3. recurse once with the updated messages

  ### Question

  Is the current behavior intentional, or is this a bug in the continuation logic for multiple client tool invocations in a streamed step?

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create an agent that can emit multiple client-side tool invocations in a streamed step.
  2. Call it through native @mastra/client-js using MastraClient.getAgent(...).stream(...).
  3. Pass at least one clientTools entry with an execute(...) function.
  4. Use a prompt that causes the model to issue more than one client tool invocation before it can finish the response.
  5. Observe the client continuation path when the stream finishes with finishReason === 'tool-calls'.

  A minimal repro pattern is:

  - the assistant emits multiple tool-invocation parts in one streamed assistant message
  - those tool invocations correspond to client tools
  - the client should continue after tool execution

  Example high-level shape:

```typescript
  const agent = mastraClient.getAgent('myAgent');

  await agent.stream(
    [{ role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'run multiple client tool operations' }] }],
    {
      clientTools: {
        my_client_tool: {
          type: 'function',
          parameters: { /* valid schema */ },
          async execute(args) {
            return { ok: true, args };
          },
        },
      },
      memory: {
        resource: 'resource-1',
        thread: 'thread-1',
      },
    },
  );
```

  The important part is that the model emits multiple client tool invocations during the streamed step.

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

can be provided, if necessary

### Expected Behavior

When a streamed step ends with finishReason === 'tool-calls', the client should:

  1. collect all pending tool-invocation parts from the assistant message for that step
  2. execute each matching client tool exactly once
  3. patch all returned results into the assistant message
  4. make a single continuation call with the fully updated message set
  5. continue until there are no pending client tool calls left

  The run should not stop early with unfinished or cancelled client tool calls just because multiple client tool invocations were emitted in the same step.

### Environment Information

```block
System:
    OS: macOS 26.4.1
    CPU: (12) arm64 Apple M2 Max
    Shell: /bin/zsh

  Binaries:
    Node: 24.14.1
    Yarn: 4.13.0
    npm: 11.11.0

  Browsers:
    Chrome: 147.0.7727.56

  Mastra Packages:
    mastra: 1.3.15
    @mastra/auth: 1.0.2
    @mastra/client-js: 1.10.0
    @mastra/core: 1.16.0
    @mastra/deployer: 1.16.0
    @mastra/evals: 1.1.2
    @mastra/express: 1.3.0
    @mastra/loggers: 1.0.3
    @mastra/mcp: 1.3.1
    @mastra/memory: 1.10.0
    @mastra/observability: 1.5.1
    @mastra/pg: 1.8.3

```

title: Tool execution errors stored as successful results — lost on history reload
bug: onAbort callback receives empty steps and no partial text when stream is aborted mid-generation
body:
## Bug Description

When a user cancels an in-progress LLM stream, the `onAbort` callback receives `{ steps: [] }` with no accumulated text, even if the model had already generated a partial response before cancellation.

## Steps to Reproduce

```ts
const result = await agent.stream(messages, {
  abortSignal: controller.signal,
  onAbort: (event) => {
    console.log(event.text)  // undefined — partial text is lost
    console.log(event.steps) // [] — always empty
  },
})

// abort mid-stream
controller.abort()
```

## Expected Behavior

`onAbort` should receive the text that was generated before the abort signal fired:

```ts
onAbort: ({ steps, text }) => {
  console.log(text) // "Hello, I can help you with..." (partial response)
}
```

## Actual Behavior

`text` is `undefined` and `steps` is always `[]`, regardless of how much text was generated before cancellation.

## Root Cause

In `llm-execution-step.ts`, both abort code paths construct the abort event without reading `runState.state.textDeltas`, so accumulated text is never included in the event payload.

## Impact

Applications that want to save or display partial responses when users cancel generation cannot do so — the generated text is silently discarded.

title: Mastra Platform Studio does not reflect deployed server state
body:
## Bug Report

### Environment
- **Mastra version**: 1.6.0
- **Platform**: Mastra Cloud (managed hosting)
- **Project**: `staffhive.server.mastra.cloud` / `staffhive.studio.mastra.cloud`
- **Node**: 22
- **OS**: Windows 11

### Description

After a successful `npx mastra server deploy --yes`, the **Server** works correctly (health check passes, agent streaming works, memory with PostgresStore works), but the **Studio** (`*.studio.mastra.cloud`) does not reflect the deployed state:

1. **Editor tab not functional** — `MastraEditor()` is configured in the Mastra instance, but the Studio does not recognize it. Cannot edit system prompts, variables, or tools through the Studio UI.

2. **Memory/Storage not recognized** — The server correctly uses `PostgresStore` (with SSL) and handles `resourceId`/`threadId` requests without error. However, the Studio shows no indication that storage is configured. Agent interactions through the Studio return: 
   ```
   MastraClientError: HTTP error! status: 500 - Memory requires a storage provider to function.
   ```
   ...even though the same endpoint works when called directly via `curl`.

3. **Observability/Traces not showing** — `@mastra/observability` v1.9.1 is configured with `DefaultExporter`, `CloudExporter`, and `SensitiveDataFilter`. The deploy succeeds, but Studio shows no traces, evaluations, or observability data.

4. **Tools, workflows, and workspace not recognized** — The Studio doesn't display the agent's registered tools, despite the server's `/api/agents` endpoint correctly listing them all.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Mastra instance with `PostgresStore`, `MastraEditor`, and `Observability`
2. Deploy with `npx mastra server deploy --yes`
3. Verify server health: `curl https://<project>.server.mastra.cloud/health` → `{"success":true}`
4. Verify agents: `curl https://<project>.server.mastra.cloud/api/agents` → returns full agent config with tools
5. Test streaming: `curl -X POST https://<project>.server.mastra.cloud/api/agents/qualification-agent/stream` with `resourceId`/`threadId` → works correctly
6. Open Studio at `https://<project>.studio.mastra.cloud` → none of the above is reflected

### Expected Behavior

Studio should reflect the same state as the deployed Server — showing configured tools, editor, memory/storage, and observability features.

### Actual Behavior

Studio appears to be running a stale or disconnected instance. Server works perfectly; Studio does not recognize any of the configured features.

### Workaround

Running `npx mastra dev` locally at `localhost:4111` works correctly — Editor, tools, memory, and all features are visible and functional. The issue is specific to the cloud-hosted Studio.

### Additional Context

We also experienced a separate issue where deploy failures show only `Deploy failed: Node.js v22.22.2` with no container runtime logs. title: Observability: `toModelOutput` return value is never captured in traces
body:
This issue was created from Discord post 1494999893314502798:

[![Open in Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open_in_Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/channels/1309558646228779139/1494999893314502798)

**Problem**

  When a tool defines `toModelOutput` (the transformer that shapes what the LLM actually sees), its return value is not recorded in any span. Every observability surface — Mastra Studio, `/api/observability/traces/:id`, Langfuse exporter — only shows the raw `execute()` output.

**Why it matters**

  Given a tool with `toModelOutput`, traces cannot distinguish between:

  1. `toModelOutput` is never invoked.
  2. It runs but returns unchanged data.
  3. It runs and transforms the payload the LLM reads.

  All three produce identical spans. For non-trivial transformers (redaction, enrichment, reshaping, schema wrapping), this leaves no way to verify the model received the intended content without manual `console.log` or a custom OTel exporter.

**Environment**

  - `@mastra/core` 1.25.0, `@mastra/observability` 1.9.1
  - Exporters: Mastra Studio default, `@mastra/langfuse`
  - Standard v5 streaming path

**Proposed fix**

  Expose the already-computed `providerMetadata.mastra.modelOutput` as a span attribute on the `tool_call` span (e.g. `mastra.tool.modelOutput`), ideally behind an opt-in `captureToolModelOutput` flag on `Observability`. Zero extra compute — only serialization cost gated by the flag.

**Minimal repro**

  ```ts
  export const echoTool = createTool({
    id: 'echo',
    inputSchema: z.object({ text: z.string() }),
    outputSchema: z.object({ text: z.string() }),
    execute: async ({ text }) => ({ text }),
    toModelOutput: (output) => ({
      type: 'json' as const,
      value: { text: output.text, _marker: 'TRANSFORMED' },
    }),
  });

  After invoking the agent, _marker appears in no span — even though the LLM receives it.
  ```

title: [Parity] Evented workflow engine: parallel multi-suspend coordination (skipped shared tests, processWorkflowSuspend active-path TODO)
body:
### Describe the Bug

There is a documented parity gap between the default workflow engine and the evented engine around parallel workflows where multiple branches can `suspend()`.

In the monorepo, this shows up as:
- `packages/core/src/workflows/evented/evented-workflow.test.ts` skips `resumeParallelMulti` and `resumeMultiSuspendError`, with a comment that parallel suspend has a race-related concern (each branch can publish `workflow.suspend` independently).
- `processWorkflowSuspend` in `packages/core/src/workflows/evented/workflow-event-processor/index.ts` contains a TODO: "if there are still active paths don't end the workflow yet" before publishing `workflows-finish`, without an `activeSteps`-style guard analogous to the foreach path (which waits / aggregates before emitting suspend-related events in the "check if all iterations are complete" logic).

I do **not** have a minimal user script where the **final** workflow result differs between engines for the basic parallel double-suspend scenario. A small public repro completes with `[OK]` and matching numeric results on both `--engine=default` and `--engine=evented`. The concern is **event ordering / coordination / parity** and un-skipping the shared suite, not a simple "wrong final output" in that script.

Related (not duplicates): [#6418](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/6418) / [#6423](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/6423) addressed **resume** completion semantics for parallel steps; this report is about **evented** suspend/finish **coordination** and **shared test** coverage.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the minimal repro (no Mastra monorepo required):

   git clone https://github.com/h30s/mastra_repo.git
   cd mastra_repo
   npm install

2. Run:

   npx tsx src/repro.ts --engine=evented
   npx tsx src/repro.ts --engine=default

3. For **internal** context (maintainers / contributors), open:
   - `packages/core/src/workflows/evented/evented-workflow.test.ts`  `skipTests.resumeParallelMulti` and `resumeMultiSuspendError`
   - `packages/core/src/workflows/evented/workflow-event-processor/index.ts`  `processWorkflowSuspend` and the TODO above `workflows-finish`

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://github.com/h30s/mastra_repo

### Expected Behavior

The evented engine should coordinate parallel suspend/finish semantics with the same guarantees as the default engine for the scenarios covered by the shared workflow test suite (e.g. `resumeParallelMulti`, `resumeMultiSuspendError`).

Concretely: `processWorkflowSuspend` should be audited against parallel `activeSteps` / sibling-branch state so `workflows-finish` / suspend-related pub/sub emissions are not emitted while other parallel paths are still active, similar in spirit to foreach’s "don’t emit until concurrent work is reconciled" logic.

Once fixed, the evented engine should be able to run those shared tests without skipping them, and behavior should match the default engine for these cases.

title: [BUG] Suspended tool approvals don't round-trip as v6 UI parts on reload
body:
### Describe the Bug

## Summary

When an agent suspends waiting on `requireApproval`, the approval state is parked in message `metadata.pendingToolApprovals` and the stored tool part stays at `state: 'input-available'`. As a result, `toAISdkMessages(storedMessages, { version: 'v6' })` returns a message that the AI SDK v6 `useChat` hook can't render as an approval — the `tool-approval-request` part is nowhere on the message, and there's no `approvalId` for `approve()` / `deny()` to target.

This breaks the "reload mid-approval" UX: if a user refreshes the page while a tool is pending approval, the UI sees a tool that looks like it's just mid-execution.



## Root cause

PRs #14592 and #15345 cover the v6 surface, but leave a seam:

- **#14592** (MessageList v6 + `toAISdkMessages`): shape-to-shape adapter. Preserves v6 approval parts if they're on the message, but doesn't synthesize them.
- **#15345** (native v6 approval streaming): emits `tool-approval-request` **during** the stream and auto-detects `approval-responded` on resubmit. Doesn't touch persistence or replay.

Neither PR bridges the gap because Mastra's agent loop persists the suspension state as `metadata.pendingToolApprovals` — a sidecar — rather than mutating the tool part to `state: 'approval-requested'` with an `approvalId`. `AIV6Adapter` has nothing to preserve on output because the approval-ness isn't in the parts.

## Current workaround

Downstream consumers have to re-implement (b) themselves on the read path. Example shim:

```js
for (const msg of messages) {
  const approvals = msg.metadata?.pendingToolApprovals
  if (!approvals) continue
  for (const { toolCallId, runId } of Object.values(approvals)) {
    const part = (msg.parts || []).find(p => p.toolCallId === toolCallId)
    if (!part || part.state === 'output-available' || part.output) continue
    part.state = 'approval-requested'
    part.approval = { id: `${runId}::${toolCallId}` }
  }
}
```

## Versions

- `@mastra/ai-sdk@1.4.1-alpha.1`
- `@mastra/core@1.26.0-alpha.2`

## Related

- #14592 — Versioned `toAISdkMessages` / MessageList v6 support
- #15345 — Native v6 approval flow on streaming + resume detection

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure a tool with `requireApproval: true`.
2. Stream a turn that calls it — client gets `tool-approval-request` correctly (fixed by #15345).
3. **Before approving, reload the page.**
4. Fetch the thread's messages and run through `toAISdkMessages(..., { version: 'v6' })`.
5. Observe: the last assistant message has `state: 'input-available'` on the tool part, `approval` field is missing, and `metadata.pendingToolApprovals` carries `runId` / `toolCallId` / `resumeSchema`.


### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

N/A

### Expected Behavior

Expected: the tool part comes back as

```json
{
  "type": "tool-<name>",
  "state": "approval-requested",
  "approval": { "id": "<runId>::<toolCallId>" },
  "input": { ... }
}
```

so `useChat` can render approval UI and `approve()` / `deny()` resolve against a known `approvalId`.

### Environment Information

```block
N/A
```

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

title: Support providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl on ModelMessages (continuation of #13849)
body:
## Summary

`@mastra/core` does not propagate `providerOptions` set on messages (rolling cache breakpoints) through its UI→Model message conversion pipeline, making it impossible to cache the message history against Anthropic's ephemeral prompt cache. This blocks the most impactful cost-reduction lever for long-running agent loops.

Issue #13849 tracked the same underlying problem but was closed in March 2026 without a code fix — the workaround suggested (`processInputStep`) is known to be broken when the agent produces assistant messages with tool_calls (index mis-mapping in `aiV5UIMessagesToAIV5ModelMessages`), which is the normal mode of operation for any tool-using agent.

## Setup

- `@mastra/core@1.24.1`
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.68`
- Agent with tools + `maxSteps: 50`
- Claude Opus 4.6

## Expected

Setting `providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl` on a `ModelMessage` (or on a content part inside one) should reach the provider. The underlying `@ai-sdk/anthropic` already supports `cache_control` on 7 message/part shapes — the bottleneck is purely Mastra stripping `providerOptions` during the UI→Model conversion.

## Actual

- `providerOptions` on `instructions` (system message): propagated ✓
- `providerOptions` on tool `createTool({ ... providerOptions })`: propagated ✓
- `providerOptions` on messages in the conversation history: stripped ✗

Observable effect: in a 50-step ticket resolution trace, `cache_read` is constant at ~11k tokens (only the system prompt + tools), while `prompt_total` grows to 67k+ tokens by step 50 — cache hit rate falls from ~92% at step 1 to ~14% at step 50, because the accumulated history is never cached.

## Repro

Minimal reproduction: an agent with any tool + memory enabled, interacting through more than 2-3 turns. Inspect the outgoing Anthropic request — no `cache_control` markers appear on any message object even if `providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl` is set via input processor or any other path.

## Current workaround

We ship a custom `LanguageModelV3Middleware` that runs at the prompt-final stage (after all UI→Model conversion), marking the last message with `cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }`. This works (cache hit rate goes from ~17% to ~70%+ in our internal testing) but requires bypassing Mastra's agent config and wrapping the model directly.

Wrapping pattern (~30 LoC): we reimplemented a minimal `wrapLanguageModel` using only `@ai-sdk/provider` types to avoid pulling in the full `ai` package as a dependency. This is brittle because it sits outside the framework's public surface.

## Proposal

Either:

1. **Fix the index-mapping bug** in `aiV5UIMessagesToAIV5ModelMessages` so `processInputStep` becomes usable with tool_call messages, AND document it as the supported path for per-message cache markers.
2. **Expose an agent-level prompt-final hook** (equivalent to `wrapLanguageModel` / `transformParams`) so users don't need to bypass the framework to modify the final payload.
3. **Auto-apply rolling cache breakpoints on the last user/assistant message when a message has `cacheControl: ephemeral` anywhere in its provider options** — zero-config path for the common case.

Happy to contribute a PR if the team points at the preferred direction.
